**Surah 74 (al-Muddaththir), verses 1–7**

Meccan (revealed in Mecca), and it has one thousand and ten letters, two hundred and fifty words, and fifty-six verses.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Ahmad informed me, saying: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Abu Amr al-Khayri and Amr ibn Abdullah al-Basri related to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus related to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surah al-Muddaththir will be given the reward of ten good deeds for each person who believed in Muhammad and who denied him in Mecca." [50] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/171.]]

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾: that is, the one wrapped up in his cloak.

Abu Nu'aym al-Isfara'ini informed us, saying: Abu Imran ibn Musa ibn al-Abbas al-Aradawari informed us, saying: Al-Abbas ibn al-Walid ibn Mazid al-Bayruti informed us in Beirut, saying: My father informed me, saying: Abu Amr al-Awza'i related to us, saying: Abu Nasr Yahya ibn Abi Kathir al-Attar al-Yamani related to us, saying: I asked Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman: "Which part of the Qur'an was revealed first?" He said:

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I stayed in seclusion on Hira' for a month. When my period of seclusion ended, I descended and went down into the valley. I was called, so I looked before me, behind me, to my right and to my left, and I saw nothing. Then I looked up at the sky, and there he was, upon the Throne, in the air. Fear seized me, so I told them, and they wrapped me up. Then God, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾, until: ﴿And your garments, purify﴾." [51] [[Sahih Muslim: 1/99, with variation.]]

Abu Nu'aym also related to us, saying: Abu Imran related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Amir al-Baghdadi related to us, saying: Sa'd Abu Muhammad related to us, saying: Shaybān related to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: Jabir ibn Abdullah informed me that the first thing revealed of the Qur'an was ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾. Jabir said: Shall I not tell you what I heard from the Prophet (peace be upon him)? I heard him say: "I stayed in seclusion on Hira'. When my period of seclusion ended, I went along the bottom of the valley, and a caller called me. I looked to my right, my left, behind me and in front of me, and I saw nothing. Then he called me again, and I looked up, and there he was, sitting on a throne between the sky and the earth. I trembled with fear and went to Khadija and said: 'Wrap me up, and pour cold water over me.' Then God, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾." [52] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 29/179.]]

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Yazid al-Sayrafi informed us, saying: Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Yahya al-Madani related to us, from Yunus, from al-Zuhri, who said: I heard Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman say: Jabir informed me that he heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) say: "Revelation came upon me once, and while I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my eyes toward the sky, and there was the angel who had come to me at Hira', sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. I trembled with fear until I fell to the ground. I went to my family and said: 'Cover me up.' So God, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾." [53] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 5/100; Asbab al-Nuzul al-Wahidi: 7, with variation.]]

﴿Arise and warn, and glorify your Lord, and purify your garments﴾. Ikrima said: Ibn Abbas was asked about this verse, and he said: It means: do not wear them for disobedience or for treachery. Then he said, quoting Ghaylan ibn Salama al-Thaqafi:

"By the praise of God, I have not worn a sinner's garment,
nor have I covered myself with treachery."

The Arabs say of a man who keeps his word and is truthful: "He has clean garments," and of one who betrays and breaks his word: "He has filthy garments."

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: Do not wear them for treachery, nor for injustice, nor for filth; wear them while you are pure. Qatada, Ibrahim, al-Dahhak, al-Sha'bi, al-Zuhri and Yaman said: ﴿And your garments, purify﴾ means from sin, wrongdoing and disobedience. The scholars of meaning (ahl al-ma'ani) said: He intended: purify yourself from sins, and he referred to the body by the garments because they enclose it, as in the words of Antara:

"I pierced with the spear his thick garment,
and the noble man is not forbidden from the spear's point,"

meaning himself. Another said:

"The garments of the Banu Awf are clean and pure,
and their faces are white, bright like the traveler's torch,"

meaning the persons of the Banu Awf.

al-Suddi said: It is said of a man when he is righteous: "He has pure garments," and when he is wicked: "He has foul garments." The poet said:

"O God, verily Amir ibn Jahm,
or he who blames the Hajj, in greasy garments,"

meaning: soiled with sins.

Abu Zawq, from al-Dahhak: ﴿And your deeds, make right﴾. This is also the report of Fudayl ibn Iyad, from Mansur, from Mujahid.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿And your heart and your house, purify﴾. The evidence for this interpretation is the words of Imru' al-Qays:

"If I have displeased you with some conduct of mine,
then ask my garments about your garments, which will come loose."

meaning: my heart, from your heart.

al-Hasan and al-Muqarrazi said: ﴿And your character, beautify﴾. Their evidence is the words of a poet:

"Yahya is not blamed for bad character,
Yahya is pure of garments, free."

meaning: of good character.

Ata' from Ibn Abbas: Do not let your garments be from earnings that are of no value. Ibn Zayd and Ibn Shurayk said: Shake out your garments, wash them with water, and purify them from impurity, because the polytheists did not purify themselves, so He commanded him to purify his garments.

al-Farra' said: I heard some of them say: purify them with alkali (ushnan).

Tawus said: ﴿And your garments, shorten and tuck up﴾, because shortening garments is a purification of them. It was also said: ﴿And your family, purify﴾, meaning purify them from sins by admonition and discipline. The Arabs call a family a garment, a covering, and a wrap, and this has been mentioned before. Yahya ibn Mu'adh said: Purify your heart from the disease of sins and the preoccupations of this world, and you will find the sweetness of worship, for whoever does not preserve the body does not find desire for food. It was also said: Purify your heart from all other than God.

﴿And the abomination, forsake﴾. al-Hasan, Ikrima, Mujahid, Humayd, Abu Ja'far, Shayba and Ya'qub read (wa-l-rujza) with a damma on the ra'. The same was transmitted by al-Fadl and Hafs from Asim, and Abu Hatim chose it. The rest read it with a kasra on the ra', and Abu Ubayd chose it, saying: because it is the more widespread and more common of the two dialects, and the two are dialects with the same meaning.

Ibn Abbas said: Abandon sin. Mujahid, Qatada, Ikrima, al-Zuhri and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿And idols, forsake﴾, and do not approach them. This is also the report of al-Walibi from Ibn Abbas. It was also said that the zay in it is a substitute for the sin, and the Arabs interchange the zay and the sin because their points of articulation are close. The evidence for this interpretation is His words, glorified is He: ﴿So shun the abomination of idols﴾ [[Surah al-Hajj: 30.]].

Abu al-Aliya and al-Rabi' said: al-rujz with a damma means the idol, and with a kasra means impurity and disobedience. al-Dahhak said: It means polytheism. Ibn Kaysan said: It means the devil. al-Kalbi said: It means punishment. The meaning of the verse is: forsake the deeds that make punishment due to you. It was also said: Remove love of this world from your heart, for it is the root of every sin. It was also said: and your soul, oppose it.

﴿And do not bestow favor seeking more﴾. The common reading is with the doubling made clear. Abu al-Sammak al-Adawi read (wa-la tamunn) with idgham (assimilation) and a fatha, emphasized. al-Hasan read (tastakthiru) in the jussive as an answer to the prohibition, and this is weak because it is not an answer. al-A'mash read it in the accusative, as if he assumed the lam of purpose, as though he said: "in order that you may seek more." The rest read it in the nominative. They differed about the meaning of the verse. Most exegetes said: Do not give anything in order to receive something greater. Qatada said: Do not give anything out of desire for worldly recompense and exchange. al-Qurazi said: Do not give your wealth out of flattery. al-Dahhak and Mujahid said: This was specific to the Prophet (ﷺ). al-Dahhak also said: There are two kinds of ostentation, permissible and forbidden. As for the permissible, it is gifts; as for the forbidden, it is usury.

al-Hasan said: ﴿And do not bestow favor﴾ upon God by your deed, so that you consider it great. al-Rabi' said: Let your deed not appear great in your eyes, for what God has bestowed and given you is little. Ibn Kaysan said: Do not regard your deed as great, lest you see it as coming from yourself, when your deed is in fact a favor from God, glorified is He, upon you, since He made a way for you to worship Him and gave you the guidance to do so. Khasif from Mujahid: "and do not weaken" (wa-la tadh'af) in seeking to increase good, from their saying "a strong rope" when it is weak. Its evidence is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "and do not bestow favor that you may seek more." Ibn Zayd said: The meaning is: do not bestow prophethood upon people, so that you take from them a reward and worldly wealth in return for it. Zayd ibn Aslam said: When you give a gift, give it for your Lord, and be patient until He is the one who rewards you for it. Mujahid said: ﴿And be patient for your Lord, for what you have suffered﴾. Ibn Zayd said: You have borne a great matter, fighting the Arabs and then the non-Arabs, so be patient in it for God's sake. It was also said: be patient for the sake of God's commands and prohibitions. It was also said: ﴿So be patient﴾ beneath the courses of decree, for God's sake. It was also said: abandon blame and weariness. It was also said: ﴿So be patient﴾ in trial, for He tests His beloved and His chosen ones.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Ahmad informed me, saying: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Abu Amr al-Khayri and Amr ibn Abdullah al-Basri related to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus related to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surah al-Muddaththir will be given the reward of ten good deeds for each person who believed in Muhammad and who denied him in Mecca." [50] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/171.]]

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾: that is, the one wrapped up in his cloak.

Abu Nu'aym al-Isfara'ini informed us, saying: Abu Imran ibn Musa ibn al-Abbas al-Aradawari informed us, saying: Al-Abbas ibn al-Walid ibn Mazid al-Bayruti informed us in Beirut, saying: My father informed me, saying: Abu Amr al-Awza'i related to us, saying: Abu Nasr Yahya ibn Abi Kathir al-Attar al-Yamani related to us, saying: I asked Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman: "Which part of the Qur'an was revealed first?" He said:

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I stayed in seclusion on Hira' for a month. When my period of seclusion ended, I descended and went down into the valley. I was called, so I looked before me, behind me, to my right and to my left, and I saw nothing. Then I looked up at the sky, and there he was, upon the Throne, in the air. Fear seized me, so I told them, and they wrapped me up. Then God, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾, until: ﴿And your garments, purify﴾." [51] [[Sahih Muslim: 1/99, with variation.]]

Abu Nu'aym also related to us, saying: Abu Imran related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Amir al-Baghdadi related to us, saying: Sa'd Abu Muhammad related to us, saying: Shaybān related to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: Jabir ibn Abdullah informed me that the first thing revealed of the Qur'an was ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾. Jabir said: Shall I not tell you what I heard from the Prophet (peace be upon him)? I heard him say: "I stayed in seclusion on Hira'. When my period of seclusion ended, I went along the bottom of the valley, and a caller called me. I looked to my right, my left, behind me and in front of me, and I saw nothing. Then he called me again, and I looked up, and there he was, sitting on a throne between the sky and the earth. I trembled with fear and went to Khadija and said: 'Wrap me up, and pour cold water over me.' Then God, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾." [52] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 29/179.]]

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Yazid al-Sayrafi informed us, saying: Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Yahya al-Madani related to us, from Yunus, from al-Zuhri, who said: I heard Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman say: Jabir informed me that he heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) say: "Revelation came upon me once, and while I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my eyes toward the sky, and there was the angel who had come to me at Hira', sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. I trembled with fear until I fell to the ground. I went to my family and said: 'Cover me up.' So God, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾." [53] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 5/100; Asbab al-Nuzul al-Wahidi: 7, with variation.]]

﴿Arise and warn, and glorify your Lord, and purify your garments﴾. Ikrima said: Ibn Abbas was asked about this verse, and he said: It means: do not wear them for disobedience or for treachery. Then he said, quoting Ghaylan ibn Salama al-Thaqafi:

"By the praise of God, I have not worn a sinner's garment,
nor have I covered myself with treachery."

The Arabs say of a man who keeps his word and is truthful: "He has clean garments," and of one who betrays and breaks his word: "He has filthy garments."

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: Do not wear them for treachery, nor for injustice, nor for filth; wear them while you are pure. Qatada, Ibrahim, al-Dahhak, al-Sha'bi, al-Zuhri and Yaman said: ﴿And your garments, purify﴾ means from sin, wrongdoing and disobedience. The scholars of meaning (ahl al-ma'ani) said: He intended: purify yourself from sins, and he referred to the body by the garments because they enclose it, as in the words of Antara:

"I pierced with the spear his thick garment,
and the noble man is not forbidden from the spear's point,"

meaning himself. Another said:

"The garments of the Banu Awf are clean and pure,
and their faces are white, bright like the traveler's torch,"

meaning the persons of the Banu Awf.

al-Suddi said: It is said of a man when he is righteous: "He has pure garments," and when he is wicked: "He has foul garments." The poet said:

"O God, verily Amir ibn Jahm,
or he who blames the Hajj, in greasy garments,"

meaning: soiled with sins.

Abu Zawq, from al-Dahhak: ﴿And your deeds, make right﴾. This is also the report of Fudayl ibn Iyad, from Mansur, from Mujahid.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿And your heart and your house, purify﴾. The evidence for this interpretation is the words of Imru' al-Qays:

"If I have displeased you with some conduct of mine,
then ask my garments about your garments, which will come loose."

meaning: my heart, from your heart.

al-Hasan and al-Muqarrazi said: ﴿And your character, beautify﴾. Their evidence is the words of a poet:

"Yahya is not blamed for bad character,
Yahya is pure of garments, free."

meaning: of good character.

Ata' from Ibn Abbas: Do not let your garments be from earnings that are of no value. Ibn Zayd and Ibn Shurayk said: Shake out your garments, wash them with water, and purify them from impurity, because the polytheists did not purify themselves, so He commanded him to purify his garments.

al-Farra' said: I heard some of them say: purify them with alkali (ushnan).

Tawus said: ﴿And your garments, shorten and tuck up﴾, because shortening garments is a purification of them. It was also said: ﴿And your family, purify﴾, meaning purify them from sins by admonition and discipline. The Arabs call a family a garment, a covering, and a wrap, and this has been mentioned before. Yahya ibn Mu'adh said: Purify your heart from the disease of sins and the preoccupations of this world, and you will find the sweetness of worship, for whoever does not preserve the body does not find desire for food. It was also said: Purify your heart from all other than God.

﴿And the abomination, forsake﴾. al-Hasan, Ikrima, Mujahid, Humayd, Abu Ja'far, Shayba and Ya'qub read (wa-l-rujza) with a damma on the ra'. The same was transmitted by al-Fadl and Hafs from Asim, and Abu Hatim chose it. The rest read it with a kasra on the ra', and Abu Ubayd chose it, saying: because it is the more widespread and more common of the two dialects, and the two are dialects with the same meaning.

Ibn Abbas said: Abandon sin. Mujahid, Qatada, Ikrima, al-Zuhri and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿And idols, forsake﴾, and do not approach them. This is also the report of al-Walibi from Ibn Abbas. It was also said that the zay in it is a substitute for the sin, and the Arabs interchange the zay and the sin because their points of articulation are close. The evidence for this interpretation is His words, glorified is He: ﴿So shun the abomination of idols﴾ [[Surah al-Hajj: 30.]].

Abu al-Aliya and al-Rabi' said: al-rujz with a damma means the idol, and with a kasra means impurity and disobedience. al-Dahhak said: It means polytheism. Ibn Kaysan said: It means the devil. al-Kalbi said: It means punishment. The meaning of the verse is: forsake the deeds that make punishment due to you. It was also said: Remove love of this world from your heart, for it is the root of every sin. It was also said: and your soul, oppose it.

﴿And do not bestow favor seeking more﴾. The common reading is with the doubling made clear. Abu al-Sammak al-Adawi read (wa-la tamunn) with idgham (assimilation) and a fatha, emphasized. al-Hasan read (tastakthiru) in the jussive as an answer to the prohibition, and this is weak because it is not an answer. al-A'mash read it in the accusative, as if he assumed the lam of purpose, as though he said: "in order that you may seek more." The rest read it in the nominative. They differed about the meaning of the verse. Most exegetes said: Do not give anything in order to receive something greater. Qatada said: Do not give anything out of desire for worldly recompense and exchange. al-Qurazi said: Do not give your wealth out of flattery. al-Dahhak and Mujahid said: This was specific to the Prophet (ﷺ). al-Dahhak also said: There are two kinds of ostentation, permissible and forbidden. As for the permissible, it is gifts; as for the forbidden, it is usury.

al-Hasan said: ﴿And do not bestow favor﴾ upon God by your deed, so that you consider it great. al-Rabi' said: Let your deed not appear great in your eyes, for what God has bestowed and given you is little. Ibn Kaysan said: Do not regard your deed as great, lest you see it as coming from yourself, when your deed is in fact a favor from God, glorified is He, upon you, since He made a way for you to worship Him and gave you the guidance to do so. Khasif from Mujahid: "and do not weaken" (wa-la tadh'af) in seeking to increase good, from their saying "a strong rope" when it is weak. Its evidence is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "and do not bestow favor that you may seek more." Ibn Zayd said: The meaning is: do not bestow prophethood upon people, so that you take from them a reward and worldly wealth in return for it. Zayd ibn Aslam said: When you give a gift, give it for your Lord, and be patient until He is the one who rewards you for it. Mujahid said: ﴿And be patient for your Lord, for what you have suffered﴾. Ibn Zayd said: You have borne a great matter, fighting the Arabs and then the non-Arabs, so be patient in it for God's sake. It was also said: be patient for the sake of God's commands and prohibitions. It was also said: ﴿So be patient﴾ beneath the courses of decree, for God's sake. It was also said: abandon blame and weariness. It was also said: ﴿So be patient﴾ in trial, for He tests His beloved and His chosen ones.

**8–31**

*Fa-idha nuqira fi al-naqur*: "When the trumpet is blown." Meaning: when it is blown into the Horn (al-sur).

Abu Muhammad al-Mukhalladi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Ahmad al-Hafuzi informed us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: Asbat ibn Muhammad al-Qurashi narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from ʿAtiyya, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Then when there is a blast on the Trumpet﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How can I be at ease, when the holder of the horn has put the horn to his mouth, bent his forehead, and is listening, waiting to be commanded to blow?" [54] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/326.]] The Companions of the Messenger of Allah said: "How should we say?"

He said: "Say: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. In Allah we put our trust.﴾" [55] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/326.]]

﴿For that Day, it will be a difficult day, not easy for the disbelievers.﴾ Abu Jaʿfar [Muhammad] al-Halqani [[As in the manuscript, and perhaps it is: al-Zarqani.]] informed us, saying: Abu al-ʿAbbas Ahmad ibn Harun al-Faqih narrated to us, saying:

ʿImran ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Hudba ibn Khalid al-Qaysi narrated to us, saying: Abu Hibab al-Qassab narrated to us, saying:

Zurara ibn Awfa led us in prayer, and when he reached the verse ﴿Then when there is a blast on the Trumpet﴾, he fell down dead. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/70; Tafsir al-Tha'alibi: 5/512.]]

﴿Leave Me with the one whom I created alone﴾: that is, I created him in his mother's womb, alone, a solitary one, having no wealth and no children. It was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi. Ibn ʿAbbas said: He used to be called "the Lone One" among his people.

﴿And to whom I gave abundant wealth﴾: that is, much. It was also said: wealth that increases in yield, such as crops, livestock, and trade. They differed regarding its amount. Mujahid and Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: a thousand dinars. Qatada said: four thousand dinars. Sufyan al-Thawri said: a million. Al-Nuʿman ibn Salim said: his wealth was land. Ibn ʿAbbas said: seven thousand mithqals of silver.

Muqatil said: He had a garden in al-Ta'if whose fruit never failed, in winter or summer; his proof is ﴿and extended shade﴾. [[Surat al-Waqia: 30.]]

Ibn Jurayj narrated from ʿAta', from ʿUmar, regarding His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And to whom I gave abundant wealth﴾, that he said: "A month's produce for a month."

﴿And sons present [with him]﴾: present with him in Makkah, not absent from him. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: They were thirteen sons. Mujahid and Qatada said: They were ten. Muqatil said: They were seven, all of them men, and they were: al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Khalid ibn al-Walid, ʿAmara ibn al-Walid, Hisham ibn al-Walid, al-ʿAs ibn al-Walid, Qays ibn al-Walid, and ʿAbd Shams ibn al-Walid. Three of them embraced Islam: Khalid, Hisham, and ʿAmara. They said: After the revelation of this verse, al-Walid remained in decline in his wealth and his children until he died.

﴿And I smoothed for him a smoothing﴾: that is, I spread out for him provision in life, spreading it out. Ibn ʿAbbas said: It means wealth, some of it upon some, just as bedding is spread out. ﴿Then he desires that I should give more﴾: he hopes that I will increase him in wealth and children, or in ease in this world. ﴿No!﴾: this cuts off the hope he was longing for. It is connected to the earlier speech. It was also said that it is an oath, meaning "truly," and that it begins a new verse.

﴿Indeed, he was hostile to Our verses﴾: obstinate. ﴿I will overwhelm him with a rugged ascent﴾: I will impose upon him a hardship of punishment, with no relief from it.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Ibn Saʿid narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Darraj informed me, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), regarding ﴿I will overwhelm him with a rugged ascent﴾, that he said: "It is a mountain in the Fire. He will be commanded to climb it; when he places his hand on it, it melts, and when he lifts it, it returns. When he places his foot on it, it melts, and when he lifts it, it returns." [56] [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/472.]]

﴿Indeed, he reflected and calculated﴾, and the verses that follow. The reason: When Allah, glorified is He, revealed to the Prophet (peace be upon him): ﴿Ha Mim. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing,...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿to Him is the final return﴾ [[Surat Ghafir: 1–3.]], the Prophet (peace be upon him) recited it in the mosque, and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira was near him, listening to his recitation. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) perceived that he was listening to his recitation, he repeated the verse. Al-Walid then went to the gathering of his people, Banu Makhzum, and said: "By Allah, I have heard from Muhammad words that are neither the speech of humans nor the speech of jinn. Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Saʿdan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr informed us that Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Ibn Hujayra, from Abu Hurayra, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Musa said to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic: 'Which of Your servants is the poorest?' Mujahid said: That is, it neither causes death nor gives life; that is, it does not leave anyone in it alive, nor does it leave anyone in it dead; rather, it burns them whenever their skins are renewed. Al-Suddi said: It spares them no flesh and leaves them no bone. Al-Dahhak said: When it seizes them, it leaves nothing of them; and when they are restored, it does not leave them until it destroys them. Every thing has a limit and weariness, except Hell.

﴿Scorching to the skin﴾: changing the skins. The Arabs say: "The sun scorched him and darkened him [lawwahathu]." A poet said:

*"You say of something the winds have scorched [lawwahathu al-samaʾim]..."* [[Fath al-Qadir: 5/327; its opening line is: "And he wonders at this, when he sees me pale."]]

Ru'ba said:

*"Its scorching has darkened him after his fleshiness and vigor, / Your scorching of the lean one that is drawn for the race."* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/78.]]

Mujahid said: It scorches the skin so that it leaves it blacker than the night. Ibn ʿAbbas and Zayd ibn Aslam said: It burns the skin. Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Lu'lu' narrated to us, saying: al-Haytham ibn Khalaf informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj ibn Jurayj narrated to us, saying: It was narrated to us, traced back to the Prophet (peace be upon him): "He described the guardians of the Fire, saying: 'It is as if their eyes are lightning, and as if their mouths are tusks, dragging their hair. Listen: the son of Abu Kabsha tells you that the guardians of the Fire are nineteen, and you are the most daring of them [aladdahum, i.e., the bravest]. Will not each ten of you be unable to overpower one man among the guardians of Hell?" Abu al-Ashudayn Kaladat ibn Khalaf ibn Asad al-Jumahi said: "I will suffice you against seventeen of them on my back, and seven on my belly; and you suffice me against two."

Then Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿And We have not made the companions of the Fire but angels﴾, not men, for who could overpower the angels? ﴿And We have not made their number but as a trial for those who disbelieve﴾, due to their denial of that and the saying of some of them: "I will suffice you against him." ﴿So that those who were given the Scripture may be certain﴾, because it is written in the Torah and the Gospel that they are nineteen.

﴿And those who believe may increase in faith, and those who were given the Scripture and the believers will have no doubt﴾: those who doubt. ﴿And those in whose hearts is disease﴾: doubt and hypocrisy. Most exegetes said this, but al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: The surah is Makkan, and there was absolutely no hypocrisy in Makkah, so the disease in this context is disbelief, not hypocrisy.

﴿What did Allah intend by this as an example?﴾: this was said only by the polytheists of Makkah. ﴿Thus Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾. ﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him﴾: the hosts of your Lord. Muqatil said: This is the answer to Abu Jahl when he said: "Does Muhammad have helpers only nineteen?"

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: ʿImran Ahmad ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sabbah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayda al-Warraq Abu Makhdura narrated to us, saying: Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Ashqar narrated to us, saying:

Hashim narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was dividing the spoils of Hunayn while Jibril was at his side. An angel came to him and said: "Your Lord commands you to do such-and-such." He said: The Prophet feared that they were a devil, so he said: "O Jibril, do you recognize him?" [59] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/83.]] He said: "He is an angel, and not every angel of your Lord is known to me."

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me, saying: Ibn Shanba narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Mirdas narrated to us, saying: Salama ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Quddus narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Awza'i say: Musa, peace be upon him, said: "O Lord, who is with You in the heaven?" **8–31**

*Fa-idha nuqira fi al-naqur*: "When the trumpet is blown." Meaning: when it is blown into the Horn (al-sur).

Abu Muhammad al-Mukhalladi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Ahmad al-Hafuzi informed us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: Asbat ibn Muhammad al-Qurashi narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from ʿAtiyya, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Then when there is a blast on the Trumpet﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How can I be at ease, when the holder of the horn has put the horn to his mouth, bent his forehead, and is listening, waiting to be commanded to blow?" [54] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/326.]] The Companions of the Messenger of Allah said: "How should we say?"

He said: "Say: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. In Allah we put our trust.﴾" [55] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/326.]]

﴿For that Day, it will be a difficult day, not easy for the disbelievers.﴾ Abu Jaʿfar [Muhammad] al-Halqani [[As in the manuscript, and perhaps it is: al-Zarqani.]] informed us, saying: Abu al-ʿAbbas Ahmad ibn Harun al-Faqih narrated to us, saying:

ʿImran ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Hudba ibn Khalid al-Qaysi narrated to us, saying: Abu Hibab al-Qassab narrated to us, saying:

Zurara ibn Awfa led us in prayer, and when he reached the verse ﴿Then when there is a blast on the Trumpet﴾, he fell down dead. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/70; Tafsir al-Tha'alibi: 5/512.]]

﴿Leave Me with the one whom I created alone﴾: that is, I created him in his mother's womb, alone, a solitary one, having no wealth and no children. It was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi. Ibn ʿAbbas said: He used to be called "the Lone One" among his people.

﴿And to whom I gave abundant wealth﴾: that is, much. It was also said: wealth that increases in yield, such as crops, livestock, and trade. They differed regarding its amount. Mujahid and Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: a thousand dinars. Qatada said: four thousand dinars. Sufyan al-Thawri said: a million. Al-Nuʿman ibn Salim said: his wealth was land. Ibn ʿAbbas said: seven thousand mithqals of silver.

Muqatil said: He had a garden in al-Ta'if whose fruit never failed, in winter or summer; his proof is ﴿and extended shade﴾. [[Surat al-Waqia: 30.]]

Ibn Jurayj narrated from ʿAta', from ʿUmar, regarding His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And to whom I gave abundant wealth﴾, that he said: "A month's produce for a month."

﴿And sons present [with him]﴾: present with him in Makkah, not absent from him. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: They were thirteen sons. Mujahid and Qatada said: They were ten. Muqatil said: They were seven, all of them men, and they were: al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Khalid ibn al-Walid, ʿAmara ibn al-Walid, Hisham ibn al-Walid, al-ʿAs ibn al-Walid, Qays ibn al-Walid, and ʿAbd Shams ibn al-Walid. Three of them embraced Islam: Khalid, Hisham, and ʿAmara. They said: After the revelation of this verse, al-Walid remained in decline in his wealth and his children until he died.

﴿And I smoothed for him a smoothing﴾: that is, I spread out for him provision in life, spreading it out. Ibn ʿAbbas said: It means wealth, some of it upon some, just as bedding is spread out. ﴿Then he desires that I should give more﴾: he hopes that I will increase him in wealth and children, or in ease in this world. ﴿No!﴾: this cuts off the hope he was longing for. It is connected to the earlier speech. It was also said that it is an oath, meaning "truly," and that it begins a new verse.

﴿Indeed, he was hostile to Our verses﴾: obstinate. ﴿I will overwhelm him with a rugged ascent﴾: I will impose upon him a hardship of punishment, with no relief from it.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Ibn Saʿid narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Darraj informed me, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), regarding ﴿I will overwhelm him with a rugged ascent﴾, that he said: "It is a mountain in the Fire. He will be commanded to climb it; when he places his hand on it, it melts, and when he lifts it, it returns. When he places his foot on it, it melts, and when he lifts it, it returns." [56] [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/472.]]

﴿Indeed, he reflected and calculated﴾, and the verses that follow. The reason: When Allah, glorified is He, revealed to the Prophet (peace be upon him): ﴿Ha Mim. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing,...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿to Him is the final return﴾ [[Surat Ghafir: 1–3.]], the Prophet (peace be upon him) recited it in the mosque, and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira was near him, listening to his recitation. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) perceived that he was listening to his recitation, he repeated the verse. Al-Walid then went to the gathering of his people, Banu Makhzum, and said: "By Allah, I have heard from Muhammad words that are neither the speech of humans nor the speech of jinn. Indeed, it has sweetness, and indeed it has a radiance. Its upper part is fruitful, and its lower part is abundant. It is elevated, and nothing is elevated above it."

Then he returned to his home. The Quraysh said: "Al-Walid has turned away from his religion! By Allah, al-Walid has turned away, and all of Quraysh will turn away." Al-Walid used to be called "the Sweet Basil of Quraysh." Abu Jahl said to them: "I will take care of him for you." So he went and sat down beside al-Walid, sorrowful. Al-Walid said to him: "Why do I see you sorrowful, my nephew?" He said: "What prevents me from not being sorrowful, when these Quraysh are collecting money for you to help you in your old age, and they claim that you have believed in the words of Muhammad, and you enter upon the son of Abu Kabsha and the son of Abu Quhafa to gain some of their food?" Al-Walid became angry and said: "Does Quraysh not know that I am the most abundant of them in wealth and children? Has Muhammad and his Companions been satisfied with food, so that they would have a surplus?" Then he rose with Abu Jahl until he came to his people's gathering, and said to them: "You claim that Muhammad is a madman. Have you ever seen him choke?" They said: "No, by Allah." He said: "You claim he is a soothsayer. Have you ever seen him foretell?" They said: "No, by Allah." He said: "You claim he is a poet. Have you ever seen him utter poetry?" They said: "No, by Allah." He said: "You claim he is a liar. Have you ever tested him with any lie?" They said: "No." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was called "the Trustworthy" before prophethood, because of his truthfulness.

They said: "Then what is he?" He reflected within himself, then looked, frowned, and said: "He is nothing but a sorcerer. Have you not seen him separate a man from his wife, his children, and his clients? So he is a sorcerer, and what he says is sorcery."

That is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, he reflected﴾ concerning Muhammad and the Qur'an, ﴿and calculated﴾ within himself what he could say about them. ﴿So may he be destroyed﴾: may he be cursed. Al-Zuhri said: "May he be punished." ﴿How he calculated﴾: in the manner of amazement, denial, and rebuke. ﴿Then may he be destroyed, how he calculated﴾; ﴿then he looked﴾; ﴿then he frowned and scowled﴾: grimaced. ﴿Then he turned away and was arrogant﴾, and said: ﴿This is nothing but magic which is transmitted﴾: it is related and narrated.

﴿This is nothing but the word of a human being﴾: meaning Yasar and Jabr, so it is an account transmitted from them. It was also said: he narrates it from Musaylima, the lord of Yamama, and it was also said: he narrates it from the people of Babylon.

﴿I will burn him in Saqar﴾: I will cause him to enter Saqar. It is not diptote, because it is a name of Hell.

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Saʿdan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr informed us that Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Ibn Hujayra, from Abu Hurayra, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Musa said to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic: 'Which of Your servants is the poorest?' He said: 'The companion of Saqar.'" [57] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/77.]]

﴿And what will make you know what Saqar is? It spares not, nor does it leave﴾: it leaves nothing within it without consuming and destroying it. Mujahid said: That is, it neither causes death nor gives life; that is, it does not leave anyone in it alive, nor does it leave anyone in it dead; rather, it burns them whenever their skins are renewed. Al-Suddi said: It spares them no flesh and leaves them no bone. Al-Dahhak said: When it seizes them, it leaves nothing of them; and when they are restored, it does not leave them until it destroys them. Every thing has a limit and weariness, except Hell.

﴿Scorching to the skin﴾: changing the skins. The Arabs say: "The sun scorched him and darkened him [lawwahathu]." A poet said:

*"You say of something the winds have scorched [lawwahathu al-samaʾim]..."* [[Fath al-Qadir: 5/327; its opening line is: "And he wonders at this, when he sees me pale."]]

Ru'ba said:

*"Its scorching has darkened him after his fleshiness and vigor, / Your scorching of the lean one that is drawn for the race."* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/78.]]

Mujahid said: It scorches the skin so that it leaves it blacker than the night. Ibn ʿAbbas and Zayd ibn Aslam said: It burns the skin. Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: It means Hell appears to them, so that they see it directly. Its parallel is ﴿And Hell is brought forth for the deviators﴾ [[Surat al-Shuʿara: 91.]]. ﴿Scorching﴾ is in the nominative as an attribute (naʿt) of ﴿Saqar﴾ in His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what Saqar is﴾. ʿAtiyya al-ʿAwfi recited ﴿lawwahatan lil-bashar﴾ with the accusative, and al-bashar is the plural of bashara (skin), and the plural of al-bashar is abshar.

﴿Over it are nineteen﴾: from among the guardians. It may be that they are nineteen categories, it may be that they are nineteen rows, it may be that they are nineteen angels specifically; and this is the view of most exegetes. This is not to be deemed strange, for if one angel takes the souls of all creation, it is more fitting that there be nineteen over the punishment of some of creation.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Lu'lu' narrated to us, saying: al-Haytham ibn Khalaf informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj ibn Jurayj narrated to us, saying: It was narrated to us, traced back to the Prophet (peace be upon him): "He described the guardians of the Fire, saying: 'It is as if their eyes are lightning, and as if their mouths are tusks, dragging their hair. Each one of them has a strength equal to the strength of both jinn and humans; one of them drives a nation, with a mountain on his neck, and he casts them into the Fire, and throws the mountain upon them.'" [58] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/79.]]

ʿAmr ibn Dinar said: One of them, with a single push, drives more into Hell than Rabiʿa and Mudar [combined]. Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatada, and al-Dahhak said: When this verse was revealed, Abu Jahl said to Quraysh: "May your mothers be bereaved! Listen: the son of Abu Kabsha tells you that the guardians of the Fire are nineteen, and you are the most daring of them [aladdahum, i.e., the bravest]. Will not each ten of you be unable to overpower one man among the guardians of Hell?" Abu al-Ashudayn Kaladat ibn Khalaf ibn Asad al-Jumahi said: "I will suffice you against seventeen of them on my back, and seven on my belly; and you suffice me against two."

Then Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿And We have not made the companions of the Fire but angels﴾, not men, for who could overpower the angels? ﴿And We have not made their number but as a trial for those who disbelieve﴾, due to their denial of that and the saying of some of them: "I will suffice you against him." ﴿So that those who were given the Scripture may be certain﴾, because it is written in the Torah and the Gospel that they are nineteen.

﴿And those who believe may increase in faith, and those who were given the Scripture and the believers will have no doubt﴾: those who doubt. ﴿And those in whose hearts is disease﴾: doubt and hypocrisy. Most exegetes said this, but al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: The surah is Makkan, and there was absolutely no hypocrisy in Makkah, so the disease in this context is disbelief, not hypocrisy.

﴿What did Allah intend by this as an example?﴾: this was said only by the polytheists of Makkah. ﴿Thus Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾. ﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him﴾: the hosts of your Lord. Muqatil said: This is the answer to Abu Jahl when he said: "Does Muhammad have helpers only nineteen?"

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: ʿImran Ahmad ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sabbah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayda al-Warraq Abu Makhdura narrated to us, saying: Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Ashqar narrated to us, saying:

Hashim narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was dividing the spoils of Hunayn while Jibril was at his side. An angel came to him and said: "Your Lord commands you to do such-and-such." He said: The Prophet feared that they were a devil, so he said: "O Jibril, do you recognize him?" [59] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/83.]] He said: "He is an angel, and not every angel of your Lord is known to me."

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me, saying: Ibn Shanba narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Mirdas narrated to us, saying: Salama ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Quddus narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Awza'i say: Musa, peace be upon him, said: "O Lord, who is with You in the heaven?" He said: "My angels." He said: "How many are they?" He said: "Twelve tribes." He said: "How many is each tribe?" He said: "The number of the dust."

﴿And it is not but a reminder to humanity﴾: that is, the Fire, is an admonition to people.

Mujahid said: It scorches the skin so that it leaves it blacker than the night. Ibn ʿAbbas and Zayd ibn Aslam said: It burns the skin. Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Lu'lu' narrated to us, saying: al-Haytham ibn Khalaf informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj ibn Jurayj narrated to us, saying: It was narrated to us, traced back to the Prophet (peace be upon him): "He described the guardians of the Fire, saying: 'It is as if their eyes are lightning, and as if their mouths are tusks, dragging their hair. ﴿What did Allah intend by this as an example?﴾: this was said only by the polytheists of Makkah. ﴿Thus Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾. ﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him﴾: the hosts of your Lord. Muqatil said: This is the answer to Abu Jahl when he said: "Does Muhammad have helpers only nineteen?"

Hashim narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was dividing the spoils of Hunayn while Jibril was at his side. Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me, saying: Ibn Shanba narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Mirdas narrated to us, saying: Salama ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Quddus narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Awza'i say: Musa, peace be upon him, said: "O Lord, who is with You in the heaven?" He said: "My angels." He said: "How many are they?" He said: "Twelve tribes." He said: "How many is each tribe?" He said: "The number of the dust."

﴿And those who believe may increase in faith, and those who were given the Scripture and the believers will have no doubt﴾: those who doubt. ﴿And those in whose hearts is disease﴾: doubt and hypocrisy. Most exegetes said this, but al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: The surah is Makkan, and there was absolutely no hypocrisy in Makkah, so the disease in this context is disbelief, not hypocrisy.

﴿What did Allah intend by this as an example?﴾: this was said only by the polytheists of Makkah. ﴿Thus Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾. ﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him﴾: the hosts of your Lord. Muqatil said: This is the answer to Abu Jahl when he said: "Does Muhammad have helpers only nineteen?"

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: ʿImran Ahmad ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sabbah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayda al-Warraq Abu Makhdura narrated to us, saying: Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Ashqar narrated to us, saying:

Hashim narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was dividing the spoils of Hunayn while Jibril was at his side. An angel came to him and said: "Your Lord commands you to do such-and-such." He said: The Prophet feared that they were a devil, so he said: "O Jibril, do you recognize him?" [59] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/83.]] He said: "He is an angel, and not every angel of your Lord is known to me."

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me, saying: Ibn Shanba narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Mirdas narrated to us, saying: Salama ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Quddus narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Awza'i say: Musa, peace be upon him, said: "O Lord, who is with You in the heaven?" He said: "My angels." He said: "How many are they?" He said: "Twelve tribes." He said: "How many is each tribe?" He said: "The number of the dust."

﴿And it is not but a reminder to humanity﴾: that is, the Fire, is an admonition to people.

﴿Nay, by the moon, and by the night when it turns back﴾ (idh adbara): meaning, when it goes away, departing. The reading of this word varies. Ibn Muhaysin, Nafi', Hamzah, Khalaf, Ya'qub and Hafs read *idh* without an alif, while the others read *adbara* with an alif, which is the opposite. Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading and said: "It is more in harmony with the word that follows it. Do you not see that He says: ﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾, so how could one be *idha* and the other *idh*?" Abu Hatim said: "There is no *idh* beside a word of swearing in the Qur'an; oaths are always followed by *idha*."

Qutrub said: Whoever reads ﴿and by the night when it turns back﴾ intends "it approaches," from the Arabs' saying *dabara fulan*, meaning he came behind me, so it is as if it came behind the day. Abu al-Duha said: Ibn 'Abbas used to criticise those who read *dabar* and said: "It is only *yudabbar* (used of) the back of a camel." Al-Farra' said: "Both are dialects: *dabbara* and *adbara*." The poet said:

*Ghazalah struck his heart with horsemen...
she left his ears like yesterday's passing (dabir)*

[Baladat al-Nisa': 129. In it: "his sights like yesterday's passing (da'ir)"; in Tarikh Dimashq (43/497): "qara'at al-'abir."]

Abu 'Amr said: *dabbara* is the dialect of Quraysh.

﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾ (idha asfara): the majority read it with an alif, meaning it lights up and approaches. Ibn al-Sumay' and 'Isa ibn al-Fadl read *safar* without an alif. Both are dialects: it is said *safar wajh fulan* and *asfar*, when his face lights up. It may also come from the saying *safarat al-mar'ah* when a woman removes her veil from her face. It may also mean the removal of darkness, as in *safara al-bayt*, he swept the house; and a broom is called *al-miksafarah*.

﴿Indeed it is one of the greatest (kubar)﴾: meaning, that the morning (or the moon) is one of the great matters. The singular of *kubar* is *kubra*. ﴿A warning to mankind﴾: meaning the Fire is a warner to mankind. Al-Hasan said: "By God, Allah has not warned with anything more terrible than it." *Nadhiran* is in the accusative of emphasis (qat') from ﴿one of the greatest﴾, because the latter is definite and *nadhiran* is indefinite.

Al-Khalil said: *al-nadhir* is a verbal noun like *al-nakir*, which is why it is applied to a feminine noun. It was also said that it is an attribute of Allah, Glorified is He, its meaning being: ﴿And We did not make the companions of the Fire except angels...﴾, ﴿a warning to mankind﴾, that is, a warning to them. Abu Razin said: "I am a warner to you from it, so beware of it." It was also said that it is an attribute of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the meaning of the speech is: ﴿O you who are wrapped up, arise and warn﴾, ﴿a warning to mankind﴾, so warn. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Zayd. Ibrahim, from Abu Ghaylah, read *nadhirun lil-bashar* with a *damma* on the *ra'*, as a predicate of an implied subject (*huwa*, "it is").

﴿For whoever among you wills to go forward (yataqaddam)﴾ in good and obedience, ﴿or to hold back (yata'akhkhar)﴾ from them in evil and disobedience. Its parallel and proof is ﴿And We have certainly known those who go forward among you﴾, meaning in good, ﴿and We have certainly known those who hold back﴾ from it. Al-Hasan said this. This is a threat to them, like His saying: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 29]. The meaning is that He is a warner to both of them together.

﴿Every soul is, for what it has earned, held in pledge (rahinah)﴾: pledged for its earnings, seized for its deeds. ﴿Except the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin)﴾: they are not held to account and are not held in pledge for their sins, but Allah forgives them and overlooks them, as He promised them. Qatadah said: "All people are shut up, except the companions of the right, and they differ concerning them."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn [Shanbah] [The word is illegible in the manuscript; what we have written is the likely reading] told us, saying: Radwan ibn Ahmad told us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Yaqzan, from Zadhan, from 'Ali concerning His saying ﴿except the companions of the right﴾: "They are the children of the Muslims."

What supports this:

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hasan told us, saying: al-Baghawi told us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd told us, saying: Abu 'Aqil informed us, from Nuhayyah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the children of the believers: where are they? He said: "In Paradise." And I asked him about the children of the polytheists, and he said: "If you wish, I will let you hear their wailing in the Fire."
[Fath al-Bari: 3/195.]

Abu Dhabyan said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "They are the angels."

Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, who said: "We and our Shi'ah are the companions of the right."

Muqatil said: "They are the people of Paradise who were on the right of Adam on the Day of the Covenant, when Allah, Glorified is He, said to them: 'These are in Paradise, and I do not care.'"

Al-Hasan said: "They are the Muslims who are sincere." And from him also: "They are those who were fortunate (mayamin) over their own souls." Ibn Kaysan said: "They are the righteous believers; they are not held in pledge, because they discharged what was upon them." Yaman said: "They are those who were able to release their pledges." Al-Hakim said: "They are those whom Allah, Glorified is He, chose for His service, so they are not included in the pledge, because they are the servants of Allah, Glorified is He, and His elect, and their earnings do not harm them." Al-Qasim said: "Every soul is taken for its earnings, of good and evil, except one who relies upon grace and mercy rather than earnings and service. So whoever relies on earnings is held in pledge by them, and whoever relies on grace is not seized."

I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: I heard Abu Bakr al-Razi say: I heard Abu 'Amr al-Bukhari say, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿Every soul is, for what it has earned, held in pledge﴾: "Then where is the escape from destiny, and how is there stability on the brink of danger?"

﴿In gardens, they will ask one another about the criminals (al-mujrimin)﴾, the polytheists: ﴿What has led you into Saqar?﴾ They will say: ﴿We were not of those who prayed, and we did not feed the needy, and we used to wade in vain talk with those who waded, and we used to deny the Day of Judgment, until there came to us the certainty (al-yaqin)﴾, meaning the thing certain, which is death.

Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, said: ﴿So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them﴾. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "The angels, the prophets, the martyrs, the righteous and all the believers will intercede, and none will remain in the Fire except four." Then he recited His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿We were not of those who prayed﴾ up to His saying ﴿the Day of Judgment﴾. Al-Hasan said: "We used to talk about how a martyr intercedes for seventy of his family members."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Mahan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad told us, saying: Thabit told us, from al-Hasan, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said:

"A man of the people of Paradise will say on the Day of Resurrection: 'My Lord, your servant so-and-so gave me a drink of water in the world, so intercede for him with me.' He will say: 'Go and bring him out of the Fire.' So he will go and search the Fire until he brings him out of it."
[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/188.]

And with an isnad from Hammad, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from 'Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from a man of the Banu Tamim, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A man of my ummah will intercede for more than the Banu Tamim."
[Musnad Ahmad: 5/366, with variation.]

Al-Hasan informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Nuh al-Bajali told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shahin told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, from 'Abdullah ibn Qays al-Asadi, from al-Harith ibn Aqshan, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Among my ummah are those whom Allah will admit to Paradise by their intercession more than the tribe of Mudar."
[Musnad Ahmad: 5/313, with variation.]

﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder (al-tadhkirah)?﴾ Here *mu'ridin* is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). It was also said: "They became those who turn away."

﴿As if they were donkeys (humur)﴾: the plural of *himar*.
﴿Startled (mustanfirah)﴾: the people of Medina, Syria and Ayyub read it with a *fatha* on the *fa'*, meaning frightened and panicked. Al-Mufaddal narrated the same from 'Asim, and Abu 'Ubayd preferred it. Others read it with a *kasra*, meaning fleeing. It is said *nafara* and *istanfara* have one meaning. Al-Farra' recited:

*Hold your donkey, for it is startled,
in the plain, asses fleeing from the lions.* [Note: the poet's line is "in the thr (?) ... ghartu" as written.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: Abu Hamid al-Mustamli told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Dhimmi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sallam al-Jumahi told us, saying: I asked Abu Sarab al-Ghanawi, who was an eloquent Bedouin and a reciter of the Qur'an: "Donkeys of what?" He said: "Donkeys startled, driven off by a lion." I said: "It is only ﴿fled from a lion﴾." He said: "Fled?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then *mustanfirah*."

﴿Fled from a lion (qaswarah)﴾: they differed concerning it. Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Ibn Kaysan said: "They are the archers." This is the narration of 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, and of Abu Dhabyan from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "They are the hunters," which is the narration of 'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Hamzah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "The mass of men."

'Aqil informed us, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jarir told us, saying: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith told me, saying: I heard my father narrate, saying: Dawud told me, saying: 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, client of the Banu Hashim, told me, who said: Ibn 'Abbas was asked about *al-qaswarah*, and he said: "It is a gathering of men. Did you not hear what so-and-so said in the Jahiliyyah:

*O daughter, be a good match for a good man:
his maternal kin are the tribe and the people of the qaswarah.*"
[Fath al-Qadir: 5/333.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Imran told us, saying: Abu 'Ubaydullah al-Makhzumi told us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah told us, from 'Amr, and from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Glorified is He, ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "It is the crowd of people."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Habash told us, saying: Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili told us, saying: Yahya ibn Ma'in told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-'Abdi, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "It is the noise of the people." Abu Hurayrah said: "It is the lion."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Mahan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Sulayman ibn Qutah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "In the language of the Arabs it is the lion; in the language of the Habashah (Abyssinians) it is *qaswarah*; in the language of the Persians it is *shir*; in the language of the Nabataeans it is *aryā*." It was also said: it is *fa'ulah* from *al-qasr*, which is subjugation, and it was named so because it subdues all beasts of prey.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Dhurayh told us, saying: Habbarah ibn Mughallis told us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la ibn Abi al-Musawir told us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "From the nets of the hunters." 'Ikrimah said: "From the darkness of the night." It was also said: it is the blackness of the beginning of the night, and the blackness of the end of the night is not called *qaswarah*. Zayd ibn Aslam said: "That is, from strong men. Every large, powerful thing among the Arabs is *qasur* and *qaswarah*." Labid said:

*When we shout a shout in our assemblies,
the men come to us, the protected, the lions.*
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/89.]

﴿Rather, each one of them wants to be given scrolls spread out (suhufan munashsharah)﴾. That is because they said: "O Muhammad, if you wish us to follow you, then bring us a book addressed especially to so-and-so and so-and-so from the Lord of the worlds, in which we are commanded to follow you." Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And we will not believe in your ascending until you bring down upon us a book that we may read﴾ [Surah al-Isra': 93]. Badhan, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: "The polytheists used to say: 'If Muhammad is truthful, let there be a cry at the head of each of us announcing his innocence and his safety from the Fire.'"

Mutar al-Warraq said: "They wanted to be given a document of acquittal without works." Al-Kalbi said: "The polytheists said: 'O Muhammad, we have heard that a man of the Children of Israel would wake up to find his sin and its expiation written at his head. So bring us something like that.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked this, and Allah, Glorified is He, revealed this verse: ﴿No! (kalla)﴾, meaning: it is not as you say and wish." It was also said: "Truly; and whatever comes to you from it, this is its meaning."

﴿Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter. No! Indeed it (innahu)﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿is a reminder (tadhkirah)﴾ and is not magic. ﴿So whoever wills may remember it. And they will not remember except that Allah wills (illa an yasha' Allah)﴾. ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, meaning: worthy that His prohibitions be feared, and worthy that He forgive whoever fears Him.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn al-Fadl told us, saying: Hadiyyah ibn Khalid told us. And 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Daqqaq and Harun ibn Muhammad both told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, saying: Hadiyyah told us, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Mu'ammari told us, saying: Hadiyyah told us, saying: Suhayl ibn Abi Hazm told us, from Thabit, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, and said: "Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am worthy that I be feared, and that none associate anything with Me, and I am worthy, for whoever fears Me, that I forgive him if he does not associate anything with Me.'"
[Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1437.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Malik told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: My father told us, saying: 'Abd al-Quddus ibn Bakr told us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Nazar al-Jariqi mention, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾: "I am worthy that My servant fear Me; and if he does not, then I am worthy to forgive him."

﴿Nay, by the moon, and by the night when it turns back﴾ (idh adbara): meaning, when it goes away, departing. The reading of this word varies. Ibn Muhaysin, Nafi', Hamzah, Khalaf, Ya'qub and Hafs read *idh* without an alif, while the others read *adbara* with an alif, which is the opposite. Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading and said: "It is more in harmony with the word that follows it. Do you not see that He says: ﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾, so how could one be *idha* and the other *idh*?" Abu Hatim said: "There is no *idh* beside a word of swearing in the Qur'an; oaths are always followed by *idha*."

Qutrub said: Whoever reads ﴿and by the night when it turns back﴾ intends "it approaches," from the Arabs' saying *dabara fulan*, meaning he came behind me, so it is as if it came behind the day. Abu al-Duha said: Ibn 'Abbas used to criticise those who read *dabar* and said: "It is only *yudabbar* (used of) the back of a camel." Al-Farra' said: "Both are dialects: *dabbara* and *adbara*." The poet said:

*Ghazalah struck his heart with horsemen...
she left his ears like yesterday's passing (dabir)*

[Baladat al-Nisa': 129. In it: "his sights like yesterday's passing (da'ir)"; in Tarikh Dimashq (43/497): "qara'at al-'abir."]

Abu 'Amr said: *dabbara* is the dialect of Quraysh.

﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾ (idha asfara): the majority read it with an alif, meaning it lights up and approaches. Ibn al-Sumay' and 'Isa ibn al-Fadl read *safar* without an alif. Both are dialects: it is said *safar wajh fulan* and *asfar*, when his face lights up. It may also come from the saying *safarat al-mar'ah* when a woman removes her veil from her face. It may also mean the removal of darkness, as in *safara al-bayt*, he swept the house; and a broom is called *al-miksafarah*.

﴿Indeed it is one of the greatest (kubar)﴾: meaning, that the morning (or the moon) is one of the great matters. The singular of *kubar* is *kubra*. ﴿A warning to mankind﴾: meaning the Fire is a warner to mankind. Al-Hasan said: "By God, Allah has not warned with anything more terrible than it." *Nadhiran* is in the accusative of emphasis (qat') from ﴿one of the greatest﴾, because the latter is definite and *nadhiran* is indefinite.

Al-Khalil said: *al-nadhir* is a verbal noun like *al-nakir*, which is why it is applied to a feminine noun. It was also said that it is an attribute of Allah, Glorified is He, its meaning being: ﴿And We did not make the companions of the Fire except angels...﴾, ﴿a warning to mankind﴾, that is, a warning to them. Abu Razin said: "I am a warner to you from it, so beware of it." It was also said that it is an attribute of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the meaning of the speech is: ﴿O you who are wrapped up, arise and warn﴾, ﴿a warning to mankind﴾, so warn. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Zayd. Ibrahim, from Abu Ghaylah, read *nadhirun lil-bashar* with a *damma* on the *ra'*, as a predicate of an implied subject (*huwa*, "it is").

﴿For whoever among you wills to go forward (yataqaddam)﴾ in good and obedience, ﴿or to hold back (yata'akhkhar)﴾ from them in evil and disobedience. Its parallel and proof is ﴿And We have certainly known those who go forward among you﴾, meaning in good, ﴿and We have certainly known those who hold back﴾ from it. Al-Hasan said this. This is a threat to them, like His saying: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 29]. The meaning is that He is a warner to both of them together.

﴿Every soul is, for what it has earned, held in pledge (rahinah)﴾: pledged for its earnings, seized for its deeds. ﴿Except the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin)﴾: they are not held to account and are not held in pledge for their sins, but Allah forgives them and overlooks them, as He promised them. Qatadah said: "All people are shut up, except the companions of the right, and they differ concerning them."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn [Shanbah] [The word is illegible in the manuscript; what we have written is the likely reading] told us, saying: Radwan ibn Ahmad told us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Yaqzan, from Zadhan, from 'Ali concerning His saying ﴿except the companions of the right﴾: "They are the children of the Muslims."

What supports this:

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hasan told us, saying: al-Baghawi told us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd told us, saying: Abu 'Aqil informed us, from Nuhayyah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the children of the believers: where are they? He said: "In Paradise." And I asked him about the children of the polytheists, and he said: "If you wish, I will let you hear their wailing in the Fire."
[Fath al-Bari: 3/195.]

Abu Dhabyan said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "They are the angels."

Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, who said: "We and our Shi'ah are the companions of the right."

Muqatil said: "They are the people of Paradise who were on the right of Adam on the Day of the Covenant, when Allah, Glorified is He, said to them: 'These are in Paradise, and I do not care.'"

Al-Hasan said: "They are the Muslims who are sincere." And from him also: "They are those who were fortunate (mayamin) over their own souls." Ibn Kaysan said: "They are the righteous believers; they are not held in pledge, because they discharged what was upon them." Yaman said: "They are those who were able to release their pledges." Al-Hakim said: "They are those whom Allah, Glorified is He, chose for His service, so they are not included in the pledge, because they are the servants of Allah, Glorified is He, and His elect, and their earnings do not harm them." Al-Qasim said: "Every soul is taken for its earnings, of good and evil, except one who relies upon grace and mercy rather than earnings and service. So whoever relies on earnings is held in pledge by them, and whoever relies on grace is not seized."

I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: I heard Abu Bakr al-Razi say: I heard Abu 'Amr al-Bukhari say, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿Every soul is, for what it has earned, held in pledge﴾: "Then where is the escape from destiny, and how is there stability on the brink of danger?"

﴿In gardens, they will ask one another about the criminals (al-mujrimin)﴾, the polytheists: ﴿What has led you into Saqar?﴾ They will say: ﴿We were not of those who prayed, and we did not feed the needy, and we used to wade in vain talk with those who waded, and we used to deny the Day of Judgment, until there came to us the certainty (al-yaqin)﴾, meaning the thing certain, which is death.

Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, said: ﴿So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them﴾. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "The angels, the prophets, the martyrs, the righteous and all the believers will intercede, and none will remain in the Fire except four." Then he recited His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿We were not of those who prayed﴾ up to His saying ﴿the Day of Judgment﴾. Al-Hasan said: "We used to talk about how a martyr intercedes for seventy of his family members."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Mahan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad told us, saying: Thabit told us, from al-Hasan, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said:

"A man of the people of Paradise will say on the Day of Resurrection: 'My Lord, your servant so-and-so gave me a drink of water in the world, so intercede for him with me.' He will say: 'Go and bring him out of the Fire.' So he will go and search the Fire until he brings him out of it."
[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/188.]

And with an isnad from Hammad, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from 'Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from a man of the Banu Tamim, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A man of my ummah will intercede for more than the Banu Tamim."
[Musnad Ahmad: 5/366, with variation.]

Al-Hasan informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Nuh al-Bajali told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shahin told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, from 'Abdullah ibn Qays al-Asadi, from al-Harith ibn Aqshan, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Among my ummah are those whom Allah will admit to Paradise by their intercession more than the tribe of Mudar."
[Musnad Ahmad: 5/313, with variation.]

﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder (al-tadhkirah)?﴾ Here *mu'ridin* is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). It was also said: "They became those who turn away."

﴿As if they were donkeys (humur)﴾: the plural of *himar*.
﴿Startled (mustanfirah)﴾: the people of Medina, Syria and Ayyub read it with a *fatha* on the *fa'*, meaning frightened and panicked. Al-Mufaddal narrated the same from 'Asim, and Abu 'Ubayd preferred it. Others read it with a *kasra*, meaning fleeing. It is said *nafara* and *istanfara* have one meaning. Al-Farra' recited:

*Hold your donkey, for it is startled,
in the plain, asses fleeing from the lions.* [Note: the poet's line is "in the thr (?) ... ghartu" as written.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: Abu Hamid al-Mustamli told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Dhimmi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sallam al-Jumahi told us, saying: I asked Abu Sarab al-Ghanawi, who was an eloquent Bedouin and a reciter of the Qur'an: "Donkeys of what?" He said: "Donkeys startled, driven off by a lion." I said: "It is only ﴿fled from a lion﴾." He said: "Fled?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then *mustanfirah*."

﴿Fled from a lion (qaswarah)﴾: they differed concerning it. Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Ibn Kaysan said: "They are the archers." This is the narration of 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, and of Abu Dhabyan from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "They are the hunters," which is the narration of 'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Hamzah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "The mass of men."

'Aqil informed us, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jarir told us, saying: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith told me, saying: I heard my father narrate, saying: Dawud told me, saying: 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, client of the Banu Hashim, told me, who said: Ibn 'Abbas was asked about *al-qaswarah*, and he said: "It is a gathering of men. Did you not hear what so-and-so said in the Jahiliyyah:

*O daughter, be a good match for a good man:
his maternal kin are the tribe and the people of the qaswarah.*"
[Fath al-Qadir: 5/333.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Imran told us, saying: Abu 'Ubaydullah al-Makhzumi told us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah told us, from 'Amr, and from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Glorified is He, ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "It is the crowd of people."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Habash told us, saying: Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili told us, saying: Yahya ibn Ma'in told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-'Abdi, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "It is the noise of the people." Abu Hurayrah said: "It is the lion."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Mahan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Sulayman ibn Qutah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "In the language of the Arabs it is the lion; in the language of the Habashah (Abyssinians) it is *qaswarah*; in the language of the Persians it is *shir*; in the language of the Nabataeans it is *aryā*." It was also said: it is *fa'ulah* from *al-qasr*, which is subjugation, and it was named so because it subdues all beasts of prey.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Dhurayh told us, saying: Habbarah ibn Mughallis told us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la ibn Abi al-Musawir told us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "From the nets of the hunters." 'Ikrimah said: "From the darkness of the night." It was also said: it is the blackness of the beginning of the night, and the blackness of the end of the night is not called *qaswarah*. Zayd ibn Aslam said: "That is, from strong men. Every large, powerful thing among the Arabs is *qasur* and *qaswarah*." Labid said:

*When we shout a shout in our assemblies,
the men come to us, the protected, the lions.*
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/89.]

﴿Rather, each one of them wants to be given scrolls spread out (suhufan munashsharah)﴾. That is because they said: "O Muhammad, if you wish us to follow you, then bring us a book addressed especially to so-and-so and so-and-so from the Lord of the worlds, in which we are commanded to follow you." Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And we will not believe in your ascending until you bring down upon us a book that we may read﴾ [Surah al-Isra': 93]. Badhan, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: "The polytheists used to say: 'If Muhammad is truthful, let there be a cry at the head of each of us announcing his innocence and his safety from the Fire.'"

Mutar al-Warraq said: "They wanted to be given a document of acquittal without works." Al-Kalbi said: "The polytheists said: 'O Muhammad, we have heard that a man of the Children of Israel would wake up to find his sin and its expiation written at his head. So bring us something like that.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked this, and Allah, Glorified is He, revealed this verse: ﴿No! (kalla)﴾, meaning: it is not as you say and wish." It was also said: "Truly; and whatever comes to you from it, this is its meaning."

﴿Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter. No! Indeed it (innahu)﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿is a reminder (tadhkirah)﴾ and is not magic. ﴿So whoever wills may remember it. And they will not remember except that Allah wills (illa an yasha' Allah)﴾. ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, meaning: worthy that His prohibitions be feared, and worthy that He forgive whoever fears Him.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn al-Fadl told us, saying: Hadiyyah ibn Khalid told us. And 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Daqqaq and Harun ibn Muhammad both told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, saying: Hadiyyah told us, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Mu'ammari told us, saying: Hadiyyah told us, saying: Suhayl ibn Abi Hazm told us, from Thabit, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, and said: "Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am worthy that I be feared, and that none associate anything with Me, and I am worthy, for whoever fears Me, that I forgive him if he does not associate anything with Me.'"
[Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1437.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Malik told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: My father told us, saying: 'Abd al-Quddus ibn Bakr told us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Nazar al-Jariqi mention, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾: "I am worthy that My servant fear Me; and if he does not, then I am worthy to forgive him."

﴿Nay, by the moon, and by the night when it turns back﴾ (idh adbara): meaning, when it goes away, departing. The reading of this word varies. Ibn Muhaysin, Nafi', Hamzah, Khalaf, Ya'qub and Hafs read *idh* without an alif, while the others read *adbara* with an alif, which is the opposite. Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading and said: "It is more in harmony with the word that follows it. Do you not see that He says: ﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾, so how could one be *idha* and the other *idh*?" Abu Hatim said: "There is no *idh* beside a word of swearing in the Qur'an; oaths are always followed by *idha*."
