Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: Abu Hamid al-Mustamli told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Dhimmi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sallam al-Jumahi told us, saying: I asked Abu Sarab al-Ghanawi, who was an eloquent Bedouin and a reciter of the Qur'an: "Donkeys of what?" He said: "Donkeys startled, driven off by a lion." I said: "It is only ﴿fled from a lion﴾." He said: "Fled?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then *mustanfirah*."

﴿Fled from a lion (qaswarah)﴾: they differed concerning it. Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Ibn Kaysan said: "They are the archers." This is the narration of 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, and of Abu Dhabyan from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "They are the hunters," which is the narration of 'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Hamzah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "The mass of men."

'Aqil informed us, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jarir told us, saying: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith told me, saying: I heard my father narrate, saying: Dawud told me, saying: 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, client of the Banu Hashim, told me, who said: Ibn 'Abbas was asked about *al-qaswarah*, and he said: "It is a gathering of men. Did you not hear what so-and-so said in the Jahiliyyah:

*O daughter, be a good match for a good man:
his maternal kin are the tribe and the people of the qaswarah.*"
[Fath al-Qadir: 5/333.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Imran told us, saying: Abu 'Ubaydullah al-Makhzumi told us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah told us, from 'Amr, and from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Glorified is He, ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "It is the crowd of people."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Habash told us, saying: Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili told us, saying: Yahya ibn Ma'in told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-'Abdi, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "It is the noise of the people." Abu Hurayrah said: "It is the lion."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Mahan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Sulayman ibn Qutah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "In the language of the Arabs it is the lion; in the language of the Habashah (Abyssinians) it is *qaswarah*; in the language of the Persians it is *shir*; in the language of the Nabataeans it is *aryā*." It was also said: it is *fa'ulah* from *al-qasr*, which is subjugation, and it was named so because it subdues all beasts of prey.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Dhurayh told us, saying: Habbarah ibn Mughallis told us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la ibn Abi al-Musawir told us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "From the nets of the hunters." 'Ikrimah said: "From the darkness of the night." It was also said: it is the blackness of the beginning of the night, and the blackness of the end of the night is not called *qaswarah*. Zayd ibn Aslam said: "That is, from strong men. Every large, powerful thing among the Arabs is *qasur* and *qaswarah*." Labid said:

*When we shout a shout in our assemblies,
the men come to us, the protected, the lions.*
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/89.]

﴿Rather, each one of them wants to be given scrolls spread out (suhufan munashsharah)﴾. That is because they said: "O Muhammad, if you wish us to follow you, then bring us a book addressed especially to so-and-so and so-and-so from the Lord of the worlds, in which we are commanded to follow you." Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And we will not believe in your ascending until you bring down upon us a book that we may read﴾ [Surah al-Isra': 93]. Badhan, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: "The polytheists used to say: 'If Muhammad is truthful, let there be a cry at the head of each of us announcing his innocence and his safety from the Fire.'"

Mutar al-Warraq said: "They wanted to be given a document of acquittal without works." Al-Kalbi said: "The polytheists said: 'O Muhammad, we have heard that a man of the Children of Israel would wake up to find his sin and its expiation written at his head. So bring us something like that.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked this, and Allah, Glorified is He, revealed this verse: ﴿No! (kalla)﴾, meaning: it is not as you say and wish." It was also said: "Truly; and whatever comes to you from it, this is its meaning."

﴿Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter. No! Indeed it (innahu)﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿is a reminder (tadhkirah)﴾ and is not magic. ﴿So whoever wills may remember it. And they will not remember except that Allah wills (illa an yasha' Allah)﴾. ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, meaning: worthy that His prohibitions be feared, and worthy that He forgive whoever fears Him.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn al-Fadl told us, saying: Hadiyyah ibn Khalid told us. And 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Daqqaq and Harun ibn Muhammad both told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, saying: Hadiyyah told us, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Mu'ammari told us, saying: Hadiyyah told us, saying: Suhayl ibn Abi Hazm told us, from Thabit, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, and said: "Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am worthy that I be feared, and that none associate anything with Me, and I am worthy, for whoever fears Me, that I forgive him if he does not associate anything with Me.'"
[Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1437.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Malik told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: My father told us, saying: 'Abd al-Quddus ibn Bakr told us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Nazar al-Jariqi mention, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾: "I am worthy that My servant fear Me; and if he does not, then I am worthy to forgive him."

﴿Nay, by the moon, and by the night when it turns back﴾ (idh adbara): meaning, when it goes away, departing. The reading of this word varies. Ibn Muhaysin, Nafi', Hamzah, Khalaf, Ya'qub and Hafs read *idh* without an alif, while the others read *adbara* with an alif, which is the opposite. Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading and said: "It is more in harmony with the word that follows it. Do you not see that He says: ﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾, so how could one be *idha* and the other *idh*?" Abu Hatim said: "There is no *idh* beside a word of swearing in the Qur'an; oaths are always followed by *idha*."

Qutrub said: Whoever reads ﴿and by the night when it turns back﴾ intends "it approaches," from the Arabs' saying *dabara fulan*, meaning he came behind me, so it is as if it came behind the day. Abu al-Duha said: Ibn 'Abbas used to criticise those who read *dabar* and said: "It is only *yudabbar* (used of) the back of a camel." Al-Farra' said: "Both are dialects: *dabbara* and *adbara*." The poet said:

*Ghazalah struck his heart with horsemen...
she left his ears like yesterday's passing (dabir)*

[Baladat al-Nisa': 129. In it: "his sights like yesterday's passing (da'ir)"; in Tarikh Dimashq (43/497): "qara'at al-'abir."]

Abu 'Amr said: *dabbara* is the dialect of Quraysh.

﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾ (idha asfara): the majority read it with an alif, meaning it lights up and approaches. Ibn al-Sumay' and 'Isa ibn al-Fadl read *safar* without an alif. Both are dialects: it is said *safar wajh fulan* and *asfar*, when his face lights up. It may also come from the saying *safarat al-mar'ah* when a woman removes her veil from her face. It may also mean the removal of darkness, as in *safara al-bayt*, he swept the house; and a broom is called *al-miksafarah*.

﴿Indeed it is one of the greatest (kubar)﴾: meaning, that the morning (or the moon) is one of the great matters. The singular of *kubar* is *kubra*. ﴿A warning to mankind﴾: meaning the Fire is a warner to mankind. Al-Hasan said: "By God, Allah has not warned with anything more terrible than it." *Nadhiran* is in the accusative of emphasis (qat') from ﴿one of the greatest﴾, because the latter is definite and *nadhiran* is indefinite.

Al-Khalil said: *al-nadhir* is a verbal noun like *al-nakir*, which is why it is applied to a feminine noun. It was also said that it is an attribute of Allah, Glorified is He, its meaning being: ﴿And We did not make the companions of the Fire except angels...﴾, ﴿a warning to mankind﴾, that is, a warning to them. Abu Razin said: "I am a warner to you from it, so beware of it." It was also said that it is an attribute of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the meaning of the speech is: ﴿O you who are wrapped up, arise and warn﴾, ﴿a warning to mankind﴾, so warn. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Zayd. Ibrahim, from Abu Ghaylah, read *nadhirun lil-bashar* with a *damma* on the *ra'*, as a predicate of an implied subject (*huwa*, "it is").

﴿For whoever among you wills to go forward (yataqaddam)﴾ in good and obedience, ﴿or to hold back (yata'akhkhar)﴾ from them in evil and disobedience. Its parallel and proof is ﴿And We have certainly known those who go forward among you﴾, meaning in good, ﴿and We have certainly known those who hold back﴾ from it. Al-Hasan said this. This is a threat to them, like His saying: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 29]. The meaning is that He is a warner to both of them together.

﴿Every soul is, for what it has earned, held in pledge (rahinah)﴾: pledged for its earnings, seized for its deeds. ﴿Except the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin)﴾: they are not held to account and are not held in pledge for their sins, but Allah forgives them and overlooks them, as He promised them. Qatadah said: "All people are shut up, except the companions of the right, and they differ concerning them."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn [Shanbah] [The word is illegible in the manuscript; what we have written is the likely reading] told us, saying: Radwan ibn Ahmad told us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Yaqzan, from Zadhan, from 'Ali concerning His saying ﴿except the companions of the right﴾: "They are the children of the Muslims."

What supports this:

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hasan told us, saying: al-Baghawi told us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd told us, saying: Abu 'Aqil informed us, from Nuhayyah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the children of the believers: where are they? He said: "In Paradise." And I asked him about the children of the polytheists, and he said: "If you wish, I will let you hear their wailing in the Fire."
[Fath al-Bari: 3/195.]

Abu Dhabyan said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "They are the angels."

Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, who said: "We and our Shi'ah are the companions of the right."

Muqatil said: "They are the people of Paradise who were on the right of Adam on the Day of the Covenant, when Allah, Glorified is He, said to them: 'These are in Paradise, and I do not care.'"

Al-Hasan said: "They are the Muslims who are sincere." And from him also: "They are those who were fortunate (mayamin) over their own souls." Ibn Kaysan said: "They are the righteous believers; they are not held in pledge, because they discharged what was upon them." Yaman said: "They are those who were able to release their pledges." Al-Hakim said: "They are those whom Allah, Glorified is He, chose for His service, so they are not included in the pledge, because they are the servants of Allah, Glorified is He, and His elect, and their earnings do not harm them." Al-Qasim said: "Every soul is taken for its earnings, of good and evil, except one who relies upon grace and mercy rather than earnings and service. So whoever relies on earnings is held in pledge by them, and whoever relies on grace is not seized."

I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: I heard Abu Bakr al-Razi say: I heard Abu 'Amr al-Bukhari say, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿Every soul is, for what it has earned, held in pledge﴾: "Then where is the escape from destiny, and how is there stability on the brink of danger?"

﴿In gardens, they will ask one another about the criminals (al-mujrimin)﴾, the polytheists: ﴿What has led you into Saqar?﴾ They will say: ﴿We were not of those who prayed, and we did not feed the needy, and we used to wade in vain talk with those who waded, and we used to deny the Day of Judgment, until there came to us the certainty (al-yaqin)﴾, meaning the thing certain, which is death.

Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, said: ﴿So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them﴾. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "The angels, the prophets, the martyrs, the righteous and all the believers will intercede, and none will remain in the Fire except four." Then he recited His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿We were not of those who prayed﴾ up to His saying ﴿the Day of Judgment﴾. Al-Hasan said: "We used to talk about how a martyr intercedes for seventy of his family members."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Mahan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad told us, saying: Thabit told us, from al-Hasan, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said:

"A man of the people of Paradise will say on the Day of Resurrection: 'My Lord, your servant so-and-so gave me a drink of water in the world, so intercede for him with me.' He will say: 'Go and bring him out of the Fire.' So he will go and search the Fire until he brings him out of it."
[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/188.]

And with an isnad from Hammad, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from 'Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from a man of the Banu Tamim, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A man of my ummah will intercede for more than the Banu Tamim."
[Musnad Ahmad: 5/366, with variation.]

Al-Hasan informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Nuh al-Bajali told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shahin told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, from 'Abdullah ibn Qays al-Asadi, from al-Harith ibn Aqshan, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Among my ummah are those whom Allah will admit to Paradise by their intercession more than the tribe of Mudar."
[Musnad Ahmad: 5/313, with variation.]

﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder (al-tadhkirah)?﴾ Here *mu'ridin* is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). It was also said: "They became those who turn away."

﴿As if they were donkeys (humur)﴾: the plural of *himar*.
﴿Startled (mustanfirah)﴾: the people of Medina, Syria and Ayyub read it with a *fatha* on the *fa'*, meaning frightened and panicked. Al-Mufaddal narrated the same from 'Asim, and Abu 'Ubayd preferred it. Others read it with a *kasra*, meaning fleeing. It is said *nafara* and *istanfara* have one meaning. Al-Farra' recited:

*Hold your donkey, for it is startled,
in the plain, asses fleeing from the lions.* [Note: the poet's line is "in the thr (?) ... ghartu" as written.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: Abu Hamid al-Mustamli told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Dhimmi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sallam al-Jumahi told us, saying: I asked Abu Sarab al-Ghanawi, who was an eloquent Bedouin and a reciter of the Qur'an: "Donkeys of what?" He said: "Donkeys startled, driven off by a lion." I said: "It is only ﴿fled from a lion﴾." He said: "Fled?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then *mustanfirah*."

﴿Fled from a lion (qaswarah)﴾: they differed concerning it. Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Ibn Kaysan said: "They are the archers." This is the narration of 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, and of Abu Dhabyan from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "They are the hunters," which is the narration of 'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Hamzah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "The mass of men."

'Aqil informed us, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jarir told us, saying: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith told me, saying: I heard my father narrate, saying: Dawud told me, saying: 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, client of the Banu Hashim, told me, who said: Ibn 'Abbas was asked about *al-qaswarah*, and he said: "It is a gathering of men. Did you not hear what so-and-so said in the Jahiliyyah:

*O daughter, be a good match for a good man:
his maternal kin are the tribe and the people of the qaswarah.*"
[Fath al-Qadir: 5/333.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Imran told us, saying: Abu 'Ubaydullah al-Makhzumi told us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah told us, from 'Amr, and from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Glorified is He, ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "It is the crowd of people."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Habash told us, saying: Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili told us, saying: Yahya ibn Ma'in told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-'Abdi, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "It is the noise of the people." Abu Hurayrah said: "It is the lion."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Mahan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Sulayman ibn Qutah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "In the language of the Arabs it is the lion; in the language of the Habashah (Abyssinians) it is *qaswarah*; in the language of the Persians it is *shir*; in the language of the Nabataeans it is *aryā*." It was also said: it is *fa'ulah* from *al-qasr*, which is subjugation, and it was named so because it subdues all beasts of prey.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Dhurayh told us, saying: Habbarah ibn Mughallis told us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la ibn Abi al-Musawir told us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "From the nets of the hunters." 'Ikrimah said: "From the darkness of the night." It was also said: it is the blackness of the beginning of the night, and the blackness of the end of the night is not called *qaswarah*. Zayd ibn Aslam said: "That is, from strong men. Every large, powerful thing among the Arabs is *qasur* and *qaswarah*." Labid said:

*When we shout a shout in our assemblies,
the men come to us, the protected, the lions.*
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/89.]

﴿Rather, each one of them wants to be given scrolls spread out (suhufan munashsharah)﴾. That is because they said: "O Muhammad, if you wish us to follow you, then bring us a book addressed especially to so-and-so and so-and-so from the Lord of the worlds, in which we are commanded to follow you." Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And we will not believe in your ascending until you bring down upon us a book that we may read﴾ [Surah al-Isra': 93]. Badhan, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: "The polytheists used to say: 'If Muhammad is truthful, let there be a cry at the head of each of us announcing his innocence and his safety from the Fire.'"

Mutar al-Warraq said: "They wanted to be given a document of acquittal without works." Al-Kalbi said: "The polytheists said: 'O Muhammad, we have heard that a man of the Children of Israel would wake up to find his sin and its expiation written at his head. So bring us something like that.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked this, and Allah, Glorified is He, revealed this verse: ﴿No! (kalla)﴾, meaning: it is not as you say and wish." It was also said: "Truly; and whatever comes to you from it, this is its meaning."

﴿Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter. No! Indeed it (innahu)﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿is a reminder (tadhkirah)﴾ and is not magic. ﴿So whoever wills may remember it. And they will not remember except that Allah wills (illa an yasha' Allah)﴾. ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, meaning: worthy that His prohibitions be feared, and worthy that He forgive whoever fears Him.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn al-Fadl told us, saying: Hadiyyah ibn Khalid told us. And 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Daqqaq and Harun ibn Muhammad both told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, saying: Hadiyyah told us, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Mu'ammari told us, saying: Hadiyyah told us, saying: Suhayl ibn Abi Hazm told us, from Thabit, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, and said: "Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am worthy that I be feared, and that none associate anything with Me, and I am worthy, for whoever fears Me, that I forgive him if he does not associate anything with Me.'"
[Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1437.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Malik told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: My father told us, saying: 'Abd al-Quddus ibn Bakr told us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Nazar al-Jariqi mention, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾: "I am worthy that My servant fear Me; and if he does not, then I am worthy to forgive him."

﴿Nay, by the moon, and by the night when it turns back﴾ (idh adbara): meaning, when it goes away, departing. The reading of this word varies. Ibn Muhaysin, Nafi', Hamzah, Khalaf, Ya'qub and Hafs read *idh* without an alif, while the others read *adbara* with an alif, which is the opposite. Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading and said: "It is more in harmony with the word that follows it. Do you not see that He says: ﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾, so how could one be *idha* and the other *idh*?" Abu Hatim said: "There is no *idh* beside a word of swearing in the Qur'an; oaths are always followed by *idha*."

Qutrub said: Whoever reads ﴿and by the night when it turns back﴾ intends "it approaches," from the Arabs' saying *dabara fulan*, meaning he came behind me, so it is as if it came behind the day. Abu al-Duha said: Ibn 'Abbas used to criticise those who read *dabar* and said: "It is only *yudabbar* (used of) the back of a camel." Al-Farra' said: "Both are dialects: *dabbara* and *adbara*." The poet said:

*Ghazalah struck his heart with horsemen...
she left his ears like yesterday's passing (dabir)*

[Baladat al-Nisa': 129. In it: "his sights like yesterday's passing (da'ir)"; in Tarikh Dimashq (43/497): "qara'at al-'abir."]

Abu 'Amr said: *dabbara* is the dialect of Quraysh.

﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾ (idha asfara): the majority read it with an alif, meaning it lights up and approaches. Ibn al-Sumay' and 'Isa ibn al-Fadl read *safar* without an alif. Both are dialects: it is said *safar wajh fulan* and *asfar*, when his face lights up. It may also come from the saying *safarat al-mar'ah* when a woman removes her veil from her face. It may also mean the removal of darkness, as in *safara al-bayt*, he swept the house; and a broom is called *al-miksafarah*.

﴿Indeed it is one of the greatest (kubar)﴾: meaning, that the morning (or the moon) is one of the great matters. The singular of *kubar* is *kubra*. ﴿A warning to mankind﴾: meaning the Fire is a warner to mankind. Al-Hasan said: "By God, Allah has not warned with anything more terrible than it." *Nadhiran* is in the accusative of emphasis (qat') from ﴿one of the greatest﴾, because the latter is definite and *nadhiran* is indefinite.

Al-Khalil said: *al-nadhir* is a verbal noun like *al-nakir*, which is why it is applied to a feminine noun. It was also said that it is an attribute of Allah, Glorified is He, its meaning being: ﴿And We did not make the companions of the Fire except angels...﴾, ﴿a warning to mankind﴾, that is, a warning to them. Abu Razin said: "I am a warner to you from it, so beware of it." It was also said that it is an attribute of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the meaning of the speech is: ﴿O you who are wrapped up, arise and warn﴾, ﴿a warning to mankind﴾, so warn. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Zayd. Ibrahim, from Abu Ghaylah, read *nadhirun lil-bashar* with a *damma* on the *ra'*, as a predicate of an implied subject (*huwa*, "it is").

﴿For whoever among you wills to go forward (yataqaddam)﴾ in good and obedience, ﴿or to hold back (yata'akhkhar)﴾ from them in evil and disobedience. Its parallel and proof is ﴿And We have certainly known those who go forward among you﴾, meaning in good, ﴿and We have certainly known those who hold back﴾ from it. Al-Hasan said this. This is a threat to them, like His saying: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 29]. The meaning is that He is a warner to both of them together.

﴿Every soul is, for what it has earned, held in pledge (rahinah)﴾: pledged for its earnings, seized for its deeds. ﴿Except the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin)﴾: they are not held to account and are not held in pledge for their sins, but Allah forgives them and overlooks them, as He promised them. Qatadah said: "All people are shut up, except the companions of the right, and they differ concerning them."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn [Shanbah] [The word is illegible in the manuscript; what we have written is the likely reading] told us, saying: Radwan ibn Ahmad told us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Yaqzan, from Zadhan, from 'Ali concerning His saying ﴿except the companions of the right﴾: "They are the children of the Muslims."

What supports this:

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hasan told us, saying: al-Baghawi told us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd told us, saying: Abu 'Aqil informed us, from Nuhayyah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the children of the believers: where are they? He said: "In Paradise." And I asked him about the children of the polytheists, and he said: "If you wish, I will let you hear their wailing in the Fire."
[Fath al-Bari: 3/195.]

Abu Dhabyan said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "They are the angels."

Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, who said: "We and our Shi'ah are the companions of the right."

Muqatil said: "They are the people of Paradise who were on the right of Adam on the Day of the Covenant, when Allah, Glorified is He, said to them: 'These are in Paradise, and I do not care.'"

Al-Hasan said: "They are the Muslims who are sincere." And from him also: "They are those who were fortunate (mayamin) over their own souls." Ibn Kaysan said: "They are the righteous believers; they are not held in pledge, because they discharged what was upon them." Yaman said: "They are those who were able to release their pledges." Al-Hakim said: "They are those whom Allah, Glorified is He, chose for His service, so they are not included in the pledge, because they are the servants of Allah, Glorified is He, and His elect, and their earnings do not harm them." Al-Qasim said: "Every soul is taken for its earnings, of good and evil, except one who relies upon grace and mercy rather than earnings and service. So whoever relies on earnings is held in pledge by them, and whoever relies on grace is not seized."

I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: I heard Abu Bakr al-Razi say: I heard Abu 'Amr al-Bukhari say, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿Every soul is, for what it has earned, held in pledge﴾: "Then where is the escape from destiny, and how is there stability on the brink of danger?"

﴿In gardens, they will ask one another about the criminals (al-mujrimin)﴾, the polytheists: ﴿What has led you into Saqar?﴾ They will say: ﴿We were not of those who prayed, and we did not feed the needy, and we used to wade in vain talk with those who waded, and we used to deny the Day of Judgment, until there came to us the certainty (al-yaqin)﴾, meaning the thing certain, which is death.

Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, said: ﴿So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them﴾. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "The angels, the prophets, the martyrs, the righteous and all the believers will intercede, and none will remain in the Fire except four." Then he recited His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿We were not of those who prayed﴾ up to His saying ﴿the Day of Judgment﴾. Al-Hasan said: "We used to talk about how a martyr intercedes for seventy of his family members."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Mahan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad told us, saying: Thabit told us, from al-Hasan, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said:

"A man of the people of Paradise will say on the Day of Resurrection: 'My Lord, your servant so-and-so gave me a drink of water in the world, so intercede for him with me.' He will say: 'Go and bring him out of the Fire.' So he will go and search the Fire until he brings him out of it."
[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/188.]

And with an isnad from Hammad, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from 'Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from a man of the Banu Tamim, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A man of my ummah will intercede for more than the Banu Tamim."
[Musnad Ahmad: 5/366, with variation.]

Al-Hasan informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Nuh al-Bajali told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shahin told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, from 'Abdullah ibn Qays al-Asadi, from al-Harith ibn Aqshan, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Among my ummah are those whom Allah will admit to Paradise by their intercession more than the tribe of Mudar."
[Musnad Ahmad: 5/313, with variation.]

﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder (al-tadhkirah)?﴾ Here *mu'ridin* is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). It was also said: "They became those who turn away."

﴿As if they were donkeys (humur)﴾: the plural of *himar*.
﴿Startled (mustanfirah)﴾: the people of Medina, Syria and Ayyub read it with a *fatha* on the *fa'*, meaning frightened and panicked. Al-Mufaddal narrated the same from 'Asim, and Abu 'Ubayd preferred it. Others read it with a *kasra*, meaning fleeing. It is said *nafara* and *istanfara* have one meaning. Al-Farra' recited:

*Hold your donkey, for it is startled,
in the plain, asses fleeing from the lions.* [Note: the poet's line is "in the thr (?) ... ghartu" as written.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: Abu Hamid al-Mustamli told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Dhimmi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sallam al-Jumahi told us, saying: I asked Abu Sarab al-Ghanawi, who was an eloquent Bedouin and a reciter of the Qur'an: "Donkeys of what?" He said: "Donkeys startled, driven off by a lion." I said: "It is only ﴿fled from a lion﴾." He said: "Fled?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then *mustanfirah*."

﴿Fled from a lion (qaswarah)﴾: they differed concerning it. Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Ibn Kaysan said: "They are the archers." This is the narration of 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, and of Abu Dhabyan from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "They are the hunters," which is the narration of 'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Hamzah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "The mass of men."

'Aqil informed us, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jarir told us, saying: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith told me, saying: I heard my father narrate, saying: Dawud told me, saying: 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, client of the Banu Hashim, told me, who said: Ibn 'Abbas was asked about *al-qaswarah*, and he said: "It is a gathering of men. Did you not hear what so-and-so said in the Jahiliyyah:

*O daughter, be a good match for a good man:
his maternal kin are the tribe and the people of the qaswarah.*"
[Fath al-Qadir: 5/333.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Imran told us, saying: Abu 'Ubaydullah al-Makhzumi told us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah told us, from 'Amr, and from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Glorified is He, ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "It is the crowd of people."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Habash told us, saying: Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili told us, saying: Yahya ibn Ma'in told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-'Abdi, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "It is the noise of the people." Abu Hurayrah said: "It is the lion."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Mahan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Sulayman ibn Qutah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "In the language of the Arabs it is the lion; in the language of the Habashah (Abyssinians) it is *qaswarah*; in the language of the Persians it is *shir*; in the language of the Nabataeans it is *aryā*." It was also said: it is *fa'ulah* from *al-qasr*, which is subjugation, and it was named so because it subdues all beasts of prey.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Dhurayh told us, saying: Habbarah ibn Mughallis told us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la ibn Abi al-Musawir told us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "From the nets of the hunters." 'Ikrimah said: "From the darkness of the night." It was also said: it is the blackness of the beginning of the night, and the blackness of the end of the night is not called *qaswarah*. Zayd ibn Aslam said: "That is, from strong men. Every large, powerful thing among the Arabs is *qasur* and *qaswarah*." Labid said:

*When we shout a shout in our assemblies,
the men come to us, the protected, the lions.*
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/89.]

﴿Rather, each one of them wants to be given scrolls spread out (suhufan munashsharah)﴾. That is because they said: "O Muhammad, if you wish us to follow you, then bring us a book addressed especially to so-and-so and so-and-so from the Lord of the worlds, in which we are commanded to follow you." Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And we will not believe in your ascending until you bring down upon us a book that we may read﴾ [Surah al-Isra': 93]. Badhan, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: "The polytheists used to say: 'If Muhammad is truthful, let there be a cry at the head of each of us announcing his innocence and his safety from the Fire.'"

Mutar al-Warraq said: "They wanted to be given a document of acquittal without works." Al-Kalbi said: "The polytheists said: 'O Muhammad, we have heard that a man of the Children of Israel would wake up to find his sin and its expiation written at his head. So bring us something like that.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked this, and Allah, Glorified is He, revealed this verse: ﴿No! (kalla)﴾, meaning: it is not as you say and wish." It was also said: "Truly; and whatever comes to you from it, this is its meaning."

﴿Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter. No! Indeed it (innahu)﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿is a reminder (tadhkirah)﴾ and is not magic. ﴿So whoever wills may remember it. And they will not remember except that Allah wills (illa an yasha' Allah)﴾. ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, meaning: worthy that His prohibitions be feared, and worthy that He forgive whoever fears Him.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn al-Fadl told us, saying: Hadiyyah ibn Khalid told us. And 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Daqqaq and Harun ibn Muhammad both told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, saying: Hadiyyah told us, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Mu'ammari told us, saying: Hadiyyah told us, saying: Suhayl ibn Abi Hazm told us, from Thabit, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, and said: "Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am worthy that I be feared, and that none associate anything with Me, and I am worthy, for whoever fears Me, that I forgive him if he does not associate anything with Me.'"
[Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1437.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Malik told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: My father told us, saying: 'Abd al-Quddus ibn Bakr told us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Nazar al-Jariqi mention, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾: "I am worthy that My servant fear Me; and if he does not, then I am worthy to forgive him."

﴿Nay, by the moon, and by the night when it turns back﴾ (idh adbara): meaning, when it goes away, departing. The reading of this word varies. Ibn Muhaysin, Nafi', Hamzah, Khalaf, Ya'qub and Hafs read *idh* without an alif, while the others read *adbara* with an alif, which is the opposite. Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading and said: "It is more in harmony with the word that follows it. Do you not see that He says: ﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾, so how could one be *idha* and the other *idh*?" Abu Hatim said: "There is no *idh* beside a word of swearing in the Qur'an; oaths are always followed by *idha*."

Qutrub said: Whoever reads ﴿and by the night when it turns back﴾ intends "it approaches," from the Arabs' saying *dabara fulan*, meaning he came behind me, so it is as if it came behind the day. Abu al-Duha said: Ibn 'Abbas used to criticise those who read *dabar* and said: "It is only *yudabbar* (used of) the back of a camel." Al-Farra' said: "Both are dialects: *dabbara* and *adbara*." The poet said:

*Ghazalah struck his heart with horsemen...
she left his ears like yesterday's passing (dabir)*

[Baladat al-Nisa': 129. In it: "his sights like yesterday's passing (da'ir)"; in Tarikh Dimashq (43/497): "qara'at al-'abir."]

Abu 'Amr said: *dabbara* is the dialect of Quraysh.

﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾ (idha asfara): the majority read it with an alif, meaning it lights up and approaches. Ibn al-Sumay' and 'Isa ibn al-Fadl read *safar* without an alif. Both are dialects: it is said *safar wajh fulan* and *asfar*, when his face lights up. It may also come from the saying *safarat al-mar'ah* when a woman removes her veil from her face. It may also mean the removal of darkness, as in *safara al-bayt*, he swept the house; and a broom is called *al-miksafarah*.

﴿Indeed it is one of the greatest (kubar)﴾: meaning, that the morning (or the moon) is one of the great matters. The singular of *kubar* is *kubra*. ﴿A warning to mankind﴾: meaning the Fire is a warner to mankind. Al-Hasan said: "By God, Allah has not warned with anything more terrible than it." *Nadhiran* is in the accusative of emphasis (qat') from ﴿one of the greatest﴾, because the latter is definite and *nadhiran* is indefinite.

Al-Khalil said: *al-nadhir* is a verbal noun like *al-nakir*, which is why it is applied to a feminine noun. It was also said that it is an attribute of Allah, Glorified is He, its meaning being: ﴿And We did not make the companions of the Fire except angels...﴾, ﴿a warning to mankind﴾, that is, a warning to them. Abu Razin said: "I am a warner to you from it, so beware of it." It was also said that it is an attribute of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the meaning of the speech is: ﴿O you who are wrapped up, arise and warn﴾, ﴿a warning to mankind﴾, so warn. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Zayd. Ibrahim, from Abu Ghaylah, read *nadhirun lil-bashar* with a *damma* on the *ra'*, as a predicate of an implied subject (*huwa*, "it is").

﴿For whoever among you wills to go forward (yataqaddam)﴾ in good and obedience, ﴿or to hold back (yata'akhkhar)﴾ from them in evil and disobedience. Its parallel and proof is ﴿And We have certainly known those who go forward among you﴾, meaning in good, ﴿and We have certainly known those who hold back﴾ from it. Al-Hasan said this. This is a threat to them, like His saying: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 29]. The meaning is that He is a warner to both of them together.

﴿Every soul is, for what it has earned, held in pledge (rahinah)﴾: pledged for its earnings, seized for its deeds. ﴿Except the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin)﴾: they are not held to account and are not held in pledge for their sins, but Allah forgives them and overlooks them, as He promised them. Qatadah said: "All people are shut up, except the companions of the right, and they differ concerning them."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn [Shanbah] [The word is illegible in the manuscript; what we have written is the likely reading] told us, saying: Radwan ibn Ahmad told us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Yaqzan, from Zadhan, from 'Ali concerning His saying ﴿except the companions of the right﴾: "They are the children of the Muslims."

What supports this:

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hasan told us, saying: al-Baghawi told us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd told us, saying: Abu 'Aqil informed us, from Nuhayyah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the children of the believers: where are they? He said: "In Paradise." And I asked him about the children of the polytheists, and he said: "If you wish, I will let you hear their wailing in the Fire."
[Fath al-Bari: 3/195.]

Abu Dhabyan said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "They are the angels."

Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, who said: "We and our Shi'ah are the companions of the right."

Muqatil said: "They are the people of Paradise who were on the right of Adam on the Day of the Covenant, when Allah, Glorified is He, said to them: 'These are in Paradise, and I do not care.'"

Al-Hasan said: "They are the Muslims who are sincere." And from him also: "They are those who were fortunate (mayamin) over their own souls." Ibn Kaysan said: "They are the righteous believers; they are not held in pledge, because they discharged what was upon them." Yaman said: "They are those who were able to release their pledges." Al-Hakim said: "They are those whom Allah, Glorified is He, chose for His service, so they are not included in the pledge, because they are the servants of Allah, Glorified is He, and His elect, and their earnings do not harm them." Al-Qasim said: "Every soul is taken for its earnings, of good and evil, except one who relies upon grace and mercy rather than earnings and service. So whoever relies on earnings is held in pledge by them, and whoever relies on grace is not seized."

I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: I heard Abu Bakr al-Razi say: I heard Abu 'Amr al-Bukhari say, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿Every soul is, for what it has earned, held in pledge﴾: "Then where is the escape from destiny, and how is there stability on the brink of danger?"

﴿In gardens, they will ask one another about the criminals (al-mujrimin)﴾, the polytheists: ﴿What has led you into Saqar?﴾ They will say: ﴿We were not of those who prayed, and we did not feed the needy, and we used to wade in vain talk with those who waded, and we used to deny the Day of Judgment, until there came to us the certainty (al-yaqin)﴾, meaning the thing certain, which is death.

Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, said: ﴿So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them﴾. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "The angels, the prophets, the martyrs, the righteous and all the believers will intercede, and none will remain in the Fire except four." Then he recited His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿We were not of those who prayed﴾ up to His saying ﴿the Day of Judgment﴾. Al-Hasan said: "We used to talk about how a martyr intercedes for seventy of his family members."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Mahan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad told us, saying: Thabit told us, from al-Hasan, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said:

"A man of the people of Paradise will say on the Day of Resurrection: 'My Lord, your servant so-and-so gave me a drink of water in the world, so intercede for him with me.' He will say: 'Go and bring him out of the Fire.' So he will go and search the Fire until he brings him out of it."
[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/188.]

And with an isnad from Hammad, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from 'Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from a man of the Banu Tamim, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A man of my ummah will intercede for more than the Banu Tamim."
[Musnad Ahmad: 5/366, with variation.]

Al-Hasan informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Nuh al-Bajali told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shahin told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, from 'Abdullah ibn Qays al-Asadi, from al-Harith ibn Aqshan, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Among my ummah are those whom Allah will admit to Paradise by their intercession more than the tribe of Mudar."
[Musnad Ahmad: 5/313, with variation.]

﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder (al-tadhkirah)?﴾ Here *mu'ridin* is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). It was also said: "They became those who turn away."

﴿As if they were donkeys (humur)﴾: the plural of *himar*.
﴿Startled (mustanfirah)﴾: the people of Medina, Syria and Ayyub read it with a *fatha* on the *fa'*, meaning frightened and panicked. Al-Mufaddal narrated the same from 'Asim, and Abu 'Ubayd preferred it. Others read it with a *kasra*, meaning fleeing. It is said *nafara* and *istanfara* have one meaning. Al-Farra' recited:

*Hold your donkey, for it is startled,
in the plain, asses fleeing from the lions.* [Note: the poet's line is "in the thr (?) ... ghartu" as written.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: Abu Hamid al-Mustamli told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Dhimmi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sallam al-Jumahi told us, saying: I asked Abu Sarab al-Ghanawi, who was an eloquent Bedouin and a reciter of the Qur'an: "Donkeys of what?" He said: "Donkeys startled, driven off by a lion." I said: "It is only ﴿fled from a lion﴾." He said: "Fled?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then *mustanfirah*."

﴿Fled from a lion (qaswarah)﴾: they differed concerning it. Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Ibn Kaysan said: "They are the archers." This is the narration of 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, and of Abu Dhabyan from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "They are the hunters," which is the narration of 'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Hamzah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "The mass of men."

'Aqil informed us, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jarir told us, saying: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith told me, saying: I heard my father narrate, saying: Dawud told me, saying: 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, client of the Banu Hashim, told me, who said: Ibn 'Abbas was asked about *al-qaswarah*, and he said: "It is a gathering of men. Did you not hear what so-and-so said in the Jahiliyyah:

*O daughter, be a good match for a good man:
his maternal kin are the tribe and the people of the qaswarah.*"
[Fath al-Qadir: 5/333.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Imran told us, saying: Abu 'Ubaydullah al-Makhzumi told us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah told us, from 'Amr, and from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Glorified is He, ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "It is the crowd of people."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Habash told us, saying: Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili told us, saying: Yahya ibn Ma'in told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-'Abdi, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "It is the noise of the people." Abu Hurayrah said: "It is the lion."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Mahan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Sulayman ibn Qutah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "In the language of the Arabs it is the lion; in the language of the Habashah (Abyssinians) it is *qaswarah*; in the language of the Persians it is *shir*; in the language of the Nabataeans it is *aryā*." It was also said: it is *fa'ulah* from *al-qasr*, which is subjugation, and it was named so because it subdues all beasts of prey.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Dhurayh told us, saying: Habbarah ibn Mughallis told us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la ibn Abi al-Musawir told us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "From the nets of the hunters." 'Ikrimah said: "From the darkness of the night." It was also said: it is the blackness of the beginning of the night, and the blackness of the end of the night is not called *qaswarah*. Zayd ibn Aslam said: "That is, from strong men. Every large, powerful thing among the Arabs is *qasur* and *qaswarah*." Labid said:

*When we shout a shout in our assemblies,
the men come to us, the protected, the lions.*
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/89.]

﴿Rather, each one of them wants to be given scrolls spread out (suhufan munashsharah)﴾. That is because they said: "O Muhammad, if you wish us to follow you, then bring us a book addressed especially to so-and-so and so-and-so from the Lord of the worlds, in which we are commanded to follow you." Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And we will not believe in your ascending until you bring down upon us a book that we may read﴾ [Surah al-Isra': 93]. Badhan, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: "The polytheists used to say: 'If Muhammad is truthful, let there be a cry at the head of each of us announcing his innocence and his safety from the Fire.'"

Mutar al-Warraq said: "They wanted to be given a document of acquittal without works." Al-Kalbi said: "The polytheists said: 'O Muhammad, we have heard that a man of the Children of Israel would wake up to find his sin and its expiation written at his head. So bring us something like that.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked this, and Allah, Glorified is He, revealed this verse: ﴿No! (kalla)﴾, meaning: it is not as you say and wish." It was also said: "Truly; and whatever comes to you from it, this is its meaning."

﴿Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter. No! Indeed it (innahu)﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿is a reminder (tadhkirah)﴾ and is not magic. ﴿So whoever wills may remember it. And they will not remember except that Allah wills (illa an yasha' Allah)﴾. ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, meaning: worthy that His prohibitions be feared, and worthy that He forgive whoever fears Him.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn al-Fadl told us, saying: Hadiyyah ibn Khalid told us. And 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Daqqaq and Harun ibn Muhammad both told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, saying: Hadiyyah told us, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Mu'ammari told us, saying: Hadiyyah told us, saying: Suhayl ibn Abi Hazm told us, from Thabit, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, and said: "Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am worthy that I be feared, and that none associate anything with Me, and I am worthy, for whoever fears Me, that I forgive him if he does not associate anything with Me.'"
[Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1437.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Malik told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: My father told us, saying: 'Abd al-Quddus ibn Bakr told us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Nazar al-Jariqi mention, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾: "I am worthy that My servant fear Me; and if he does not, then I am worthy to forgive him."

﴿Nay, by the moon, and by the night when it turns back﴾ (idh adbara): meaning, when it goes away, departing. The reading of this word varies. Ibn Muhaysin, Nafi', Hamzah, Khalaf, Ya'qub and Hafs read *idh* without an alif, while the others read *adbara* with an alif, which is the opposite. Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading and said: "It is more in harmony with the word that follows it. Do you not see that He says: ﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾, so how could one be *idha* and the other *idh*?" Abu Hatim said: "There is no *idh* beside a word of swearing in the Qur'an; oaths are always followed by *idha*."

Qutrub said: Whoever reads ﴿and by the night when it turns back﴾ intends "it approaches," from the Arabs' saying *dabara fulan*, meaning he came behind me, so it is as if it came behind the day. Abu al-Duha said: Ibn 'Abbas used to criticise those who read *dabar* and said: "It is only *yudabbar* (used of) the back of a camel." Al-Farra' said: "Both are dialects: *dabbara* and *adbara*." The poet said:

*Ghazalah struck his heart with horsemen...
she left his ears like yesterday's passing (dabir)*

[Baladat al-Nisa': 129. In it: "his sights like yesterday's passing (da'ir)"; in Tarikh Dimashq (43/497): "qara'at al-'abir."]

Abu 'Amr said: *dabbara* is the dialect of Quraysh.

﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾ (idha asfara): the majority read it with an alif, meaning it lights up and approaches. Ibn al-Sumay' and 'Isa ibn al-Fadl read *safar* without an alif. Both are dialects: it is said *safar wajh fulan* and *asfar*, when his face lights up. It may also come from the saying *safarat al-mar'ah* when a woman removes her veil from her face. It may also mean the removal of darkness, as in *safara al-bayt*, he swept the house; and a broom is called *al-miksafarah*.

﴿Indeed it is one of the greatest (kubar)﴾: meaning, that the morning (or the moon) is one of the great matters. The singular of *kubar* is *kubra*. ﴿A warning to mankind﴾: meaning the Fire is a warner to mankind. Al-Hasan said: "By God, Allah has not warned with anything more terrible than it." *Nadhiran* is in the accusative of emphasis (qat') from ﴿one of the greatest﴾, because the latter is definite and *nadhiran* is indefinite.

Al-Khalil said: *al-nadhir* is a verbal noun like *al-nakir*, which is why it is applied to a feminine noun. It was also said that it is an attribute of Allah, Glorified is He, its meaning being: ﴿And We did not make the companions of the Fire except angels...﴾, ﴿a warning to mankind﴾, that is, a warning to them. Abu Razin said: "I am a warner to you from it, so beware of it." It was also said that it is an attribute of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the meaning of the speech is: ﴿O you who are wrapped up, arise and warn﴾, ﴿a warning to mankind﴾, so warn. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Zayd. Ibrahim, from Abu Ghaylah, read *nadhirun lil-bashar* with a *damma* on the *ra'*, as a predicate of an implied subject (*huwa*, "it is").

﴿For whoever among you wills to go forward (yataqaddam)﴾ in good and obedience, ﴿or to hold back (yata'akhkhar)﴾ from them in evil and disobedience. Its parallel and proof is ﴿And We have certainly known those who go forward among you﴾, meaning in good, ﴿and We have certainly known those who hold back﴾ from it. Al-Hasan said this. This is a threat to them, like His saying: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 29]. The meaning is that He is a warner to both of them together.

﴿Every soul is, for what it has earned, held in pledge (rahinah)﴾: pledged for its earnings, seized for its deeds. ﴿Except the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin)﴾: they are not held to account and are not held in pledge for their sins, but Allah forgives them and overlooks them, as He promised them. Qatadah said: "All people are shut up, except the companions of the right, and they differ concerning them."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn [Shanbah] [The word is illegible in the manuscript; what we have written is the likely reading] told us, saying: Radwan ibn Ahmad told us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Yaqzan, from Zadhan, from 'Ali concerning His saying ﴿except the companions of the right﴾: "They are the children of the Muslims."

What supports this:

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hasan told us, saying: al-Baghawi told us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd told us, saying: Abu 'Aqil informed us, from Nuhayyah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the children of the believers: where are they? He said: "In Paradise." And I asked him about the children of the polytheists, and he said: "If you wish, I will let you hear their wailing in the Fire."
[Fath al-Bari: 3/195.]

Abu Dhabyan said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "They are the angels."

Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, who said: "We and our Shi'ah are the companions of the right."

Muqatil said: "They are the people of Paradise who were on the right of Adam on the Day of the Covenant, when Allah, Glorified is He, said to them: 'These are in Paradise, and I do not care.'"

Al-Hasan said: "They are the Muslims who are sincere." And from him also: "They are those who were fortunate (mayamin) over their own souls." Ibn Kaysan said: "They are the righteous believers; they are not held in pledge, because they discharged what was upon them." Yaman said: "They are those who were able to release their pledges." Al-Hakim said: "They are those whom Allah, Glorified is He, chose for His service, so they are not included in the pledge, because they are the servants of Allah, Glorified is He, and His elect, and their earnings do not harm them." Al-Qasim said: "Every soul is taken for its earnings, of good and evil, except one who relies upon grace and mercy rather than earnings and service. So whoever relies on earnings is held in pledge by them, and whoever relies on grace is not seized."

I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: I heard Abu Bakr al-Razi say: I heard Abu 'Amr al-Bukhari say, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿Every soul is, for what it has earned, held in pledge﴾: "Then where is the escape from destiny, and how is there stability on the brink of danger?"

﴿In gardens, they will ask one another about the criminals (al-mujrimin)﴾, the polytheists: ﴿What has led you into Saqar?﴾ They will say: ﴿We were not of those who prayed, and we did not feed the needy, and we used to wade in vain talk with those who waded, and we used to deny the Day of Judgment, until there came to us the certainty (al-yaqin)﴾, meaning the thing certain, which is death.

Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, said: ﴿So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them﴾. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "The angels, the prophets, the martyrs, the righteous and all the believers will intercede, and none will remain in the Fire except four." Then he recited His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿We were not of those who prayed﴾ up to His saying ﴿the Day of Judgment﴾. Al-Hasan said: "We used to talk about how a martyr intercedes for seventy of his family members."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Mahan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad told us, saying: Thabit told us, from al-Hasan, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said:

"A man of the people of Paradise will say on the Day of Resurrection: 'My Lord, your servant so-and-so gave me a drink of water in the world, so intercede for him with me.' He will say: 'Go and bring him out of the Fire.' So he will go and search the Fire until he brings him out of it."
[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/188.]

And with an isnad from Hammad, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from 'Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from a man of the Banu Tamim, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A man of my ummah will intercede for more than the Banu Tamim."
[Musnad Ahmad: 5/366, with variation.]

Al-Hasan informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Nuh al-Bajali told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shahin told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, from 'Abdullah ibn Qays al-Asadi, from al-Harith ibn Aqshan, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Among my ummah are those whom Allah will admit to Paradise by their intercession more than the tribe of Mudar."
[Musnad Ahmad: 5/313, with variation.]

﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder (al-tadhkirah)?﴾ Here *mu'ridin* is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). It was also said: "They became those who turn away."

﴿As if they were donkeys (humur)﴾: the plural of *himar*.
﴿Startled (mustanfirah)﴾: the people of Medina, Syria and Ayyub read it with a *fatha* on the *fa'*, meaning frightened and panicked. Al-Mufaddal narrated the same from 'Asim, and Abu 'Ubayd preferred it. Others read it with a *kasra*, meaning fleeing. It is said *nafara* and *istanfara* have one meaning. Al-Farra' recited:

*Hold your donkey, for it is startled,
in the plain, asses fleeing from the lions.* [Note: the poet's line is "in the thr (?) ... ghartu" as written.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: Abu Hamid al-Mustamli told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Dhimmi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sallam al-Jumahi told us, saying: I asked Abu Sarab al-Ghanawi, who was an eloquent Bedouin and a reciter of the Qur'an: "Donkeys of what?" He said: "Donkeys startled, driven off by a lion." I said: "It is only ﴿fled from a lion﴾." He said: "Fled?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then *mustanfirah*."

﴿Fled from a lion (qaswarah)﴾: they differed concerning it. Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Ibn Kaysan said: "They are the archers." This is the narration of 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, and of Abu Dhabyan from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "They are the hunters," which is the narration of 'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Hamzah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "The mass of men."

'Aqil informed us, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jarir told us, saying: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith told me, saying: I heard my father narrate, saying: Dawud told me, saying: 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, client of the Banu Hashim, told me, who said: Ibn 'Abbas was asked about *al-qaswarah*, and he said: "It is a gathering of men. Did you not hear what so-and-so said in the Jahiliyyah:

*O daughter, be a good match for a good man:
his maternal kin are the tribe and the people of the qaswarah.*"
[Fath al-Qadir: 5/333.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Imran told us, saying: Abu 'Ubaydullah al-Makhzumi told us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah told us, from 'Amr, and from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Glorified is He, ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "It is the crowd of people."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Habash told us, saying: Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili told us, saying: Yahya ibn Ma'in told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-'Abdi, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "It is the noise of the people." Abu Hurayrah said: "It is the lion."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Mahan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Sulayman ibn Qutah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "In the language of the Arabs it is the lion; in the language of the Habashah (Abyssinians) it is *qaswarah*; in the language of the Persians it is *shir*; in the language of the Nabataeans it is *aryā*." It was also said: it is *fa'ulah* from *al-qasr*, which is subjugation, and it was named so because it subdues all beasts of prey.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Dhurayh told us, saying: Habbarah ibn Mughallis told us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la ibn Abi al-Musawir told us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "From the nets of the hunters." 'Ikrimah said: "From the darkness of the night." It was also said: it is the blackness of the beginning of the night, and the blackness of the end of the night is not called *qaswarah*. Zayd ibn Aslam said: "That is, from strong men. Every large, powerful thing among the Arabs is *qasur* and *qaswarah*." Labid said:

*When we shout a shout in our assemblies,
the men come to us, the protected, the lions.*
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/89.]

﴿Rather, each one of them wants to be given scrolls spread out (suhufan munashsharah)﴾. That is because they said: "O Muhammad, if you wish us to follow you, then bring us a book addressed especially to so-and-so and so-and-so from the Lord of the worlds, in which we are commanded to follow you." Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And we will not believe in your ascending until you bring down upon us a book that we may read﴾ [Surah al-Isra': 93]. Badhan, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: "The polytheists used to say: 'If Muhammad is truthful, let there be a cry at the head of each of us announcing his innocence and his safety from the Fire.'"

Mutar al-Warraq said: "They wanted to be given a document of acquittal without works." Al-Kalbi said: "The polytheists said: 'O Muhammad, we have heard that a man of the Children of Israel would wake up to find his sin and its expiation written at his head. So bring us something like that.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked this, and Allah, Glorified is He, revealed this verse: ﴿No! (kalla)﴾, meaning: it is not as you say and wish." It was also said: "Truly; and whatever comes to you from it, this is its meaning."

﴿Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter. No! Indeed it (innahu)﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿is a reminder (tadhkirah)﴾ and is not magic. ﴿So whoever wills may remember it. And they will not remember except that Allah wills (illa an yasha' Allah)﴾. ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, meaning: worthy that His prohibitions be feared, and worthy that He forgive whoever fears Him.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn al-Fadl told us, saying: Hadiyyah ibn Khalid told us. And 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Daqqaq and Harun ibn Muhammad both told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, saying: Hadiyyah told us, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Mu'ammari told us, saying: Hadiyyah told us, saying: Suhayl ibn Abi Hazm told us, from Thabit, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, and said: "Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am worthy that I be feared, and that none associate anything with Me, and I am worthy, for whoever fears Me, that I forgive him if he does not associate anything with Me.'"
[Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1437.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Malik told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: My father told us, saying: 'Abd al-Quddus ibn Bakr told us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Nazar al-Jariqi mention, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾: "I am worthy that My servant fear Me; and if he does not, then I am worthy to forgive him."

﴿Nay, by the moon, and by the night when it turns back﴾ (idh adbara): meaning, when it goes away, departing. The reading of this word varies. Ibn Muhaysin, Nafi', Hamzah, Khalaf, Ya'qub and Hafs read *idh* without an alif, while the others read *adbara* with an alif, which is the opposite. Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading and said: "It is more in harmony with the word that follows it. Do you not see that He says: ﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾, so how could one be *idha* and the other *idh*?" Abu Hatim said: "There is no *idh* beside a word of swearing in the Qur'an; oaths are always followed by *idha*."

Qutrub said: Whoever reads ﴿and by the night when it turns back﴾ intends "it approaches," from the Arabs' saying *dabara fulan*, meaning he came behind me, so it is as if it came behind the day. Abu al-Duha said: Ibn 'Abbas used to criticise those who read *dabar* and said: "It is only *yudabbar* (used of) the back of a camel." Al-Farra' said: "Both are dialects: *dabbara* and *adbara*." The poet said:

*Ghazalah struck his heart with horsemen...
she left his ears like yesterday's passing (dabir)*

[Baladat al-Nisa': 129. In it: "his sights like yesterday's passing (da'ir)"; in Tarikh Dimashq (43/497): "qara'at al-'abir."]

Abu 'Amr said: *dabbara* is the dialect of Quraysh.

﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾ (idha asfara): the majority read it with an alif, meaning it lights up and approaches. Ibn al-Sumay' and 'Isa ibn al-Fadl read *safar* without an alif. Both are dialects: it is said *safar wajh fulan* and *asfar*, when his face lights up. It may also come from the saying *safarat al-mar'ah* when a woman removes her veil from her face. It may also mean the removal of darkness, as in *safara al-bayt*, he swept the house; and a broom is called *al-miksafarah*.

﴿Indeed it is one of the greatest (kubar)﴾: meaning, that the morning (or the moon) is one of the great matters. The singular of *kubar* is *kubra*. ﴿A warning to mankind﴾: meaning the Fire is a warner to mankind. Al-Hasan said: "By God, Allah has not warned with anything more terrible than it." *Nadhiran* is in the accusative of emphasis (qat') from ﴿one of the greatest﴾, because the latter is definite and *nadhiran* is indefinite.

Al-Khalil said: *al-nadhir* is a verbal noun like *al-nakir*, which is why it is applied to a feminine noun. It was also said that it is an attribute of Allah, Glorified is He, its meaning being: ﴿And We did not make the companions of the Fire except angels...﴾, ﴿a warning to mankind﴾, that is, a warning to them. Abu Razin said: "I am a warner to you from it, so beware of it." It was also said that it is an attribute of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the meaning of the speech is: ﴿O you who are wrapped up, arise and warn﴾, ﴿a warning to mankind﴾, so warn. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Zayd. Ibrahim, from Abu Ghaylah, read *nadhirun lil-bashar* with a *damma* on the *ra'*, as a predicate of an implied subject (*huwa*, "it is").

﴿For whoever among you wills to go forward (yataqaddam)﴾ in good and obedience, ﴿or to hold back (yata'akhkhar)﴾ from them in evil and disobedience. Its parallel and proof is ﴿And We have certainly known those who go forward among you﴾, meaning in good, ﴿and We have certainly known those who hold back﴾ from it. Al-Hasan said this. This is a threat to them, like His saying: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 29]. The meaning is that He is a warner to both of them together.

﴿Every soul is, for what it has earned, held in pledge (rahinah)﴾: pledged for its earnings, seized for its deeds. ﴿Except the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin)﴾: they are not held to account and are not held in pledge for their sins, but Allah forgives them and overlooks them, as He promised them. Qatadah said: "All people are shut up, except the companions of the right, and they differ concerning them."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn [Shanbah] [The word is illegible in the manuscript; what we have written is the likely reading] told us, saying: Radwan ibn Ahmad told us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Yaqzan, from Zadhan, from 'Ali concerning His saying ﴿except the companions of the right﴾: "They are the children of the Muslims."

What supports this:

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hasan told us, saying: al-Baghawi told us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd told us, saying: Abu 'Aqil informed us, from Nuhayyah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the children of the believers: where are they? He said: "In Paradise." And I asked him about the children of the polytheists, and he said: "If you wish, I will let you hear their wailing in the Fire."
[Fath al-Bari: 3/195.]

Abu Dhabyan said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "They are the angels."

Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, who said: "We and our Shi'ah are the companions of the right."

Muqatil said: "They are the people of Paradise who were on the right of Adam on the Day of the Covenant, when Allah, Glorified is He, said to them: 'These are in Paradise, and I do not care.'"

Al-Hasan said: "They are the Muslims who are sincere." And from him also: "They are those who were fortunate (mayamin) over their own souls." Ibn Kaysan said: "They are the righteous believers; they are not held in pledge, because they discharged what was upon them." Yaman said: "They are those who were able to release their pledges." Al-Hakim said: "They are those whom Allah, Glorified is He, chose for His service, so they are not included in the pledge, because they are the servants of Allah, Glorified is He, and His elect, and their earnings do not harm them." Al-Qasim said: "Every soul is taken for its earnings, of good and evil, except one who relies upon grace and mercy rather than earnings and service. So whoever relies on earnings is held in pledge by them, and whoever relies on grace is not seized."

I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: I heard Abu Bakr al-Razi say: I heard Abu 'Amr al-Bukhari say, concerning His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿Every soul is, for what it has earned, held in pledge﴾: "Then where is the escape from destiny, and how is there stability on the brink of danger?"

﴿In gardens, they will ask one another about the criminals (al-mujrimin)﴾, the polytheists: ﴿What has led you into Saqar?﴾ They will say: ﴿We were not of those who prayed, and we did not feed the needy, and we used to wade in vain talk with those who waded, and we used to deny the Day of Judgment, until there came to us the certainty (al-yaqin)﴾, meaning the thing certain, which is death.

Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, said: ﴿So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them﴾. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "The angels, the prophets, the martyrs, the righteous and all the believers will intercede, and none will remain in the Fire except four." Then he recited His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿We were not of those who prayed﴾ up to His saying ﴿the Day of Judgment﴾. Al-Hasan said: "We used to talk about how a martyr intercedes for seventy of his family members."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Mahan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad told us, saying: Thabit told us, from al-Hasan, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said:

"A man of the people of Paradise will say on the Day of Resurrection: 'My Lord, your servant so-and-so gave me a drink of water in the world, so intercede for him with me.' He will say: 'Go and bring him out of the Fire.' So he will go and search the Fire until he brings him out of it."
[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/188.]

And with an isnad from Hammad, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from 'Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from a man of the Banu Tamim, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A man of my ummah will intercede for more than the Banu Tamim."
[Musnad Ahmad: 5/366, with variation.]

Al-Hasan informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Nuh al-Bajali told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shahin told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, from 'Abdullah ibn Qays al-Asadi, from al-Harith ibn Aqshan, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Among my ummah are those whom Allah will admit to Paradise by their intercession more than the tribe of Mudar."
[Musnad Ahmad: 5/313, with variation.]

﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder (al-tadhkirah)?﴾ Here *mu'ridin* is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). It was also said: "They became those who turn away."

﴿As if they were donkeys (humur)﴾: the plural of *himar*.
﴿Startled (mustanfirah)﴾: the people of Medina, Syria and Ayyub read it with a *fatha* on the *fa'*, meaning frightened and panicked. Al-Mufaddal narrated the same from 'Asim, and Abu 'Ubayd preferred it. Others read it with a *kasra*, meaning fleeing. It is said *nafara* and *istanfara* have one meaning. Al-Farra' recited:

*Hold your donkey, for it is startled,
in the plain, asses fleeing from the lions.* [Note: the poet's line is "in the thr (?) ... ghartu" as written.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: Abu Hamid al-Mustamli told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Dhimmi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sallam al-Jumahi told us, saying: I asked Abu Sarab al-Ghanawi, who was an eloquent Bedouin and a reciter of the Qur'an: "Donkeys of what?" He said: "Donkeys startled, driven off by a lion." I said: "It is only ﴿fled from a lion﴾." He said: "Fled?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then *mustanfirah*."

﴿Fled from a lion (qaswarah)﴾: they differed concerning it. Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Ibn Kaysan said: "They are the archers." This is the narration of 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, and of Abu Dhabyan from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "They are the hunters," which is the narration of 'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Hamzah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿fled from a lion﴾: "The mass of men."

'Aqil informed us, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jarir told us, saying: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith told me, saying: I heard my father narrate, saying: Dawud told me, saying: 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, client of the Banu Hashim, told me, who said: Ibn 'Abbas was asked about *al-qaswarah*, and he said: "It is a gathering of men. Did you not hear what so-and-so said in the Jahiliyyah:

*O daughter, be a good match for a good man:
his maternal kin are the tribe and the people of the qaswarah.*"
[Fath al-Qadir: 5/333.]
